Priority at which the directed work is placed into the work queue initially to accomplish the work. If you do not provide a value for Priority, then the work enters the work queue at the base priority defined for the operation.
Name for a group of locations that share the same attributes for moving inventory.
Building in which the movement zone is located. A building is a warehouse entity consisting of one or more zones. Inventory and location information can be reported by building.
Text that further describes the zone.

If Yes, the movement zone supports the splitting of LPNs during an LPN transfer. When an LPN is moved out of the movement zone, if its details (sub-LPNs or detail LPNs) have different next locations on the movement path, the application prompts the user to split the LPN and the application updates the picking information for all of the sub-LPNs and detail LPNs on the LPN.If your warehouse is configured for picking to handling unit slots, then the sub handling unit (such as a tote) must be deposited individually off of the master handling unit (such as a trolley). For example, when an operator is in a location that is located in a movement zone configured for LPN splitting and the operator deposits a master handling unit LPN, the operator is prompted to scan or create an LPN for each slot deposit. When the sub handling unit in the slot is deposited, it is no longer associated with the master handling unit.If No, the zone does not support LPN splitting during an LPN transfer. If your warehouse is configured for picking to handling unit slots, then slots remain on the master handling unit during deposit.

If Yes, then when an operator splits a quantity off of an LPN during an inventory transfer or cross docking, the operator can enter a new LPN for the quantity (for example, from a roll of pre-printed labels).If No, then when an operator splits an LPN, the application generates a new LPN for the quantity that was split off from the original LPN.

If Yes, the application clears the assignment of a destination location from an LPN if the LPN is staged before being put away. When a destination location is allocated for putaway, the application reserves the location for the quantity of inventory pending to the location. By clearing the destination location, the pending quantity is removed, and the reserved space in the location can be used for other inventory. When the operator resumes putaway of the LPN, the application re-allocates a destination location for the inventory.If No, the application does not clear the assignment of a destination location from an LPN when the LPN is staged before being put away. When putaway is resumed, the operator is directed to the location that was originally reserved.

If Yes, the application should recalculate and find the most appropriate putaway location, including cross dock opportunities, when inventory is picked up from locations in the area. This is done to ensure that the most current data is used in determining a putaway location.If No, the application does not recalculate the best putaway location.

If Yes, then the application will attempt to fill a location during an emergency or demand replenishment. When a replenishment is generated to fill an order, the application also attempts to move additional product to fill the pickface. The application only attempts to move additional product so as not to create an additional move to the pickface or to surpass the capacity of the location.For example, if a pickface that has a capacity of 2,000 units has 200 remaining and an order needs 500 units, the application creates an emergency replenishment for 300 units to fill the order. However, if one load contains 1,000 units, instead of creating an emergency replenishment for 300, the application directs the entire load to the pickface during the replenishment. Once the order is filled with the 200 units originally in the location and 300 units from the replenishment, 700 units remain the pickface.Note: The application attempts to move additional inventory to a pickface in the highest quantity possible without creating a move to the pickface in addition to the moves required by the emergency or demand replenishment.If No, the application will not attempt to fill the location when generating an emergency or demand replenishment.

field: Allow Dynamic Pick Face Triggered Replenishments
description: If Yes, then when an item is stored in a dynamic pickface location in this zone and the inventory level reaches the defined replenishment minimum, the application attempts to create a triggered replenishment. An item is stored dynamically if the item's replenishment configuration specifies a movement zone but not a specific location. When the item is stored in the zone, the application dynamically selects a storage location not already associated with an item. Select Yes if you want to continue using the application-selected location for items that are stored dynamically.Note: If you select Yes and want to clear the dynamic location of inventory, you must either cancel the replenishment or move the inventory to a different location.If No, then when an item is stored in a dynamic pickface location in this zone and the inventory level reaches the defined replenishment minimum, a triggered replenishment is not created. Select No if you do not want locations in the zone to be refilled with the item was dynamically assigned to the location during a previous replenishment process.Note: This configuration only affects triggered replenishments. If additional inventory for an item in a dynamic location is needed for an order, the application can still generate an emergency replenishment to the location.

If Yes, then the application does not validate mixing restrictions when a demand replenishment is released. If you select Yes, then the application validates mixing restrictions for demand replenishments to locations in the zone when the replenishment work is unlocked. If a zone is configured for pre-inventory allocation (PIA) and if demand replenishments are configured to be created in a Locked status, it is possible for multiple demand replenishments to be created for a single location. With this field set to Yes, the application can release a demand replenishment in a Locked status to a location even if the location contains inventory that cannot be mixed with the replenishment inventory at the time of allocation. When a locked replenishment no longer violates the mixing restrictions and the location has available capacity, the application unlocks the work so that it can be performed.Note: If the replenishment work is manually unlocked, the application does not validate the mixing restrictions.Select Yes if you want to allow multiple PIA demand replenishments to be allocated for a location regardless of whether the mixing restrictions are satisfied at the time of allocation.If No, then the application validates the mixing restrictions when the replenishment inventory is allocated.

If Yes, an operator can override the application and pick a quantity greater than the application-directed value during replenishment to a location in this zone. For example, if the current quantity on hand in the destination location is completely allocated, the operator can choose to overpick during replenishment knowing that picking will deplete the quantity in the destination location. Because overpicking during replenishment could overfill a location, you may not want to enable this feature where it is not physically possible to overfill a location, such as in a narrow aisle.If No, the operator is not allowed to override the application-directed value.

If Yes, the application cancels the associated picks when an emergency or demand replenishment is cancelled, and cancels the associated replenishment, if necessary, when an order pick is cancelled. Specifically, if you select Yes, then the application cancels associated picks and replenishments in the following ways:• When an order pick cannot be fulfilled, the short allocation results in an emergency replenishment. If the replenishment pick is cancelled, then the associated short allocation (unfulfilled order pick) is also cancelled, or cancelled and reallocated, depending on the cancel code. If the unfulfilled order pick is cancelled instead, the emergency replenishment is only cancelled if no other short allocations or orders require the inventory. • When pre-inventory allocation (PIA) is used and a PIA pick cannot be fulfilled, the application creates a demand replenishment. If the demand replenishment is cancelled, then the associated PIA pick is also cancelled. If the PIA pick is cancelled instead, then the demand replenishment is only cancelled if no other outstanding picks require the inventory; the demand replenishment may also be regenerated if the PIA pick is cancelled with reallocation. If a PIA pick associated to a pending top-off, triggered, or manual replenishment is cancelled, then regardless of this configuration, the replenishment is not cancelled.Note: If an emergency replenishment or demand replenishment pick is cancelled with reallocation, the replenishment pick is cancelled, but the original unfulfilled order pick is reprocessed by the application.When an order pick or PIA pick is cancelled, the application considers this configuration for the source movement zone associated with the pick. When a demand or emergency replenishment is cancelled, the application considers this configuration for the destination movement zone.Select Yes, for example, in a zone where dynamic pickfaces are used so that if an order is cancelled, the pending replenishment to fill the dynamic pickface is also cancelled (if no other outstanding picks require the inventory). If no other inventory exists in the location, this allows the application to reuse the location for other inventory.If No, then the application does not cancel the associated order pick when a replenishment pick is cancelled, and does not cancel the associated replenishment when an order pick is cancelled.

If Yes, the application can allocate inventory out of the zone at a larger UOM that what is required for a replenishment pick. The allocated UOM is moved to an intermediate location (such as a pickup and deposit location) from which the replenishment pick can be performed. Following the pick, the remaining inventory must be returned to storage.Select Yes, for example, if inventory required for replenishment resides in a location that is only accessible by full pallet material handling equipment. The application can allocate a full pallet from a location in the zone, move it to a pickup and deposit location, and then allocate replenishment picks at a lower UOM level, such as cases. After the case picks are performed, the pallet LPN with the remaining inventory must be returned to storage.If No, then during replenishment processing, the application is not allowed to allocate inventory out of the zone at a larger UOM than what is required for a replenishment. For example, select No to prevent the application from allocating a pallet LPN from the zone to satisfy a case (sub-LPN) replenishment quantity.IMPORTANT: If this zone is the source zone for replenishments to a destination movement zone configured with the Split Replenishment Residuals field is set to Yes, then the Allocate Maximum UOM must be set to No.

If Yes, then if a replenishment pick exceeds the quantity needed for the replenishment request, and the residual inventory does not fit in the destination location, then the residual inventory can be split and directed elsewhere. If configured to do so, residual inventory can be used to fulfill cross docks; otherwise, the application runs putaway to find a location.Note: Additional configuration is required for this functionality. See Splitting replenishment residuals.For example, assume that a pickface location has a capacity of 50 eaches, and that the location currently has a quantity of 10 eaches. If an order requires 30 eaches, then the application creates a replenishment to fulfill the order. If this field is set to Yes and the application allocates more than the destination location can hold, then at the replenishment location, the application prompts the operator to deposit 40 eaches to fill the location to capacity. After the operator completes the deposit, the application processes the residual inventory from the replenishment pick. If configured to do so, the residual inventory can be used to fulfill cross dock opportunities. If there are no cross docks or that functionality is disabled, then the application runs putaway to find a location for the residual inventory. If allowed, the operator can override the application-directed location.Notes: • Splitting replenishment residuals can be used to avoid returning partial pallets to storage where they can no longer be allocated as a full pallet quantity.• If the Overfill field is set to Yes in the replenishment settings configuration, then when prompted with the deposit quantity that fills the replenishment location, the operator can override the quantity with a quantity that exceeds the location capacity. • If this field is set to Yes, then the Allocate Maximum UOM field on the source movement zone must be set to No.If No, then replenishments cannot be split.

field: Display Case Equivalent on Replenishment Split
description: If Yes, then when splitting replenishment residuals is enabled and a replenishment is split, the application displays the deposit quantity to the replenishment location in the item’s case-equivalent UOM. For example, If the location can hold 40.5 cases (45 eaches), then with this field set to Yes, the application displays a deposit quantity of 40 cases. The remaining 5 eaches that would fill the replenishment location are instead included in the residual quantity for splitting. Select Yes to ensure that replenishment deposits to locations in this zone are always completed in quantities of the case-equivalent UOM. If at least 1 case-equivalent UOM will not fit in the location, then the application displays the next smallest UOM that can fit in the location.If No, then the application displays the deposit quantity UOM based on the location’s capacity and what is needed to fill the location. For example, if the replenishment location can hold 40.5 cases, then with this field set to No, the system displays a deposit quantity of 45 eaches to fill the location. With this field set to No, operators may be required to deposit partial cases (case-equivalent UOM) to reach location capacity.

If Slotting is installed and enabled in Warehouse Management, this is the default inventory status to use when creating replenishment item configurations. This value is displayed as the default inventory status when you manually create replenishment item configurations for this movement zone. This is also the inventory status that application uses when dynamically creating replenishment item configurations during the slotting plan execution.

If Slotting is installed and enabled in Warehouse Management, this value indicates how the application determines quantity when creating replenishment item configurations for this movement zone.• Percentage: Percentage of a location's maximum capacity (defined for a location).• Units: Number of units per location. See Movement zone replenishment attributes.

Minimum value (percentage or unit quantity) representing the point at which a location should be replenished (refilled). If the amount in a location falls below the minimum value when executing a slotting plan, Warehouse Management automatically generates a replenishment to fill the location.
Maximum value (percentage or unit quantity) representing the amount to which a location should be filled during an automatic replenishment resulting from the execution of a slotting plan.

Method by which the application handles the deposit of a partial LPN to locations in the movement zone. A partial LPN is a sub-LPN (such as a case) or a detail LPN (such as an each or piece). The attachment strategy determines whether the application attaches a partial LPN of inventory to an existing LPN when a partial LPN is deposited to a location in the movement zone, and if so, how the attachment takes place.The attachment strategy only applies to the deposit of sub-LPNs and detail LPNs; full LPNs are not attached to other LPNs based on the attachment strategy. If you want all inventory to be on one LPN in a location, you must enable the attach to any strategy before the location contains any inventory.Note: The Attachment Strategy field on a movement zone and the Automatic LPN Consolidation field on a storage zone are mutually exclusive. To avoid unexpected behavior, if a location belongs to a movement zone with this field set to attach (any value besides Never Attach), then the location's storage zone must be configured with the Automatic LPN Consolidation field set to No.• Never Attach: When a partial LPN of inventory is moved to a location, a new LPN is created on which to attach or deposit the inventory. • Attach To Any: When a partial LPN of inventory is moved to a location that already contains inventory, the application attaches the inventory to any existing LPN in the location. If a location does not contain inventory, the application creates a new LPN number for the partial LPN. This strategy is typically used in movement zones that allow only case or each picking, where all the inventory resides on a single LPN.• Attach If Exists: When a partial LPN of inventory is moved to a location that already contains inventory, the application attaches the inventory to any existing LPN in the location. If a location does not contain inventory, the operator is not allowed to deposit a partial LPN in the location.• Attach If Unique: When a partial LPN of inventory is moved to a location that already contains inventory, an operator is required to identify the LPN on which the partial LPN is deposited. If a location does not contain inventory, the application creates a new LPN number for the partial LPN. This strategy is typically used in movement zones that allow LPN (pallet) picking.

If Yes, then in locations where inventory is stored in cases (sub-LPNs), the operator is allowed to directly perform each picks from and inventory counts on cases in the location without entering the inventory identifier (sub-LPN) of the source case. Instead, the operator enters a quantity. Set this field to Yes when you do not need to track the carton contents in the source location from which the operator performs counts and each (piece) picks. This field only applies to locations in which inventory is stored in cases and, for picking, only applies to each picks that are sourced from cases (sub-LPNs).Note: If this field is set to Yes and multiple sub-LPNs are deposited to a location in this zone, then the application consolidates the sub-LPNs onto a single sub-LPN. If there is inventory in the location, the deposited sub-LPNs are consolidated with the existing sub-LPN. However, the application does not consolidate sub-LPNs with serialized inventory.If No, then when picking or counting at locations used to store sub-LPNs, the operator is required to enter an inventory identifier (sub-LPN) to confirm the case that is counted or from which a quantity is picked.

If Yes, operators performing distribution deposit are required to perform an audit upon completing the deposit process for a distribution. During the audit, the operator is required to enter whether there is residual inventory on the LPN after the deposit work is completed. If there is residual inventory, the operator enters the quantity and the application compares the entered residual quantity against the expected residual quantity. If the quantities match, the audit passes and the operator is directed to place the residual inventory in a storage location determined by putaway. If the residual inventory does not match the quantity expected by the application, the audit fails and the inventory is directed to an exception location where it can be determined what caused the discrepancy in the residual inventory.If No, operators are not required to perform a distribution audit upon completing the deposit process for a distribution. You would typically select No only in situations where all of the picked inventory is expected to be distributed, such as when eaches are picked for e-commerce orders and distributed to cartons for shipment.

If Yes, then an RF message is displayed when the application cannot reserve a location in the next zone of a movement path for the entire quantity being moved. This functionality is used when the application is configured to delay reserving the next deposit location in a movement path until the operator picks up the inventory from its current location.For example, assume an operator picks up two LPNs from their current location to move them to the next zone in the movement path. If there are no locations available, the application presents a pickup and deposit (P&D) location in which all the inventory can be deposited. If a location in the next movement zone is available for depositing a partial quantity, the message indicates that locations are not available for all inventory and prompts the operator to either deposit the partial inventory to the intended zone (the remaining inventory is directed to an application-suggested P&D location), or deposit the entire quantity to the P&D location. For partial deposits, the application identifies the specific LPNs to be deposited to each location. You might select Yes if you want to give operators control over whether a partial deposit is made, and in some cases, to bypass a partial deposit so that the entire deposit to the next location can be made at one time.If No, then an RF message is not displayed. If you select No and the application cannot find any locations, the operator is directed to deposit the inventory to an application-suggested P&D location. If a location is available for a portion of the inventory, then the operator is directed to deposit a partial quantity to the location in the next movement zone and the remaining inventory to a P&D location. For partial deposits, the application identifies the specific LPNs to be deposited to each location. You might select No if it is common for processing locations to be mostly full (eliminating the extra step of operators responding to the prompt), and if you always want to deposit as much inventory as possible to the next hop location.

If Yes, the application automatically closes a shipping container when the last pick for the shipment is deposited in the container by an operator performing distribution deposit. Distribution deposit is the process of depositing picked inventory to a consolidation location in order to fulfill a distribution shipment. For example, if a distribution is for three items (requiring three picks) and the operator already deposited two picks into a shipping container, then when the operator deposits the third pick, the application automatically closes the container. Depending on the Automatic Pickup configuration for the location type, closed containers are either moved automatically to the operator's RF device or the application creates directed work for another operator to move the inventory to its next location. If there are multiple containers for the shipment, then all of the containers are closed and ready to be moved to their next location when the last pick is deposited to the final shipping container.Note: If you select Yes, then you must also configure the application to reserve locations in the distribution deposit movement zone by shipment. See Processing Location Reservation.If No, then the operator must manually close the containers for a shipment during distribution deposit.

Location to which the operator is directed to deposit unexpected residual inventory. After the operator completes the deposit work for an LPN at the required distribution locations, the operator is directed to perform an audit to determine if there is any residual inventory. During the application-generated audit, the operator enters the quantity of residual inventory, if any. The application compares the residual quantity against the expected residual quantity. If the quantities match, the audit passes and the operator is directed to place the residual inventory in a storage location determined by putaway. If the quantities do not match, the audit fails and the inventory is directed to the distribution exception location where the cause of the discrepancy can be determined.

If Yes, pallet building is allowed in the movement zone. Pallet building is a process in which cases or cartons are consolidated to create a new pallet.If No, pallet building is not allowed in the movement zone.

If Yes, indicates that this movement zone is used for pre-staging before the final staging location.A pre-stage movement zone is used in the outbound work sequencing process to provide buffer hop locations in the movement path to which picked inventory can be deposited. If a pre-stage movement zone is defined in the movement path, then pick work that would otherwise be locked at source locations (and only unlocked based on outbound work sequence) would be unlocked immediately for picking to pre-stage locations. This is done so that pick work in the work queue for smaller UOMs (which typically have a longer lead time) can be unlocked for picking but not for staging. At the pre-stage location, transfer work to staging for the picked inventory is locked in the work queue until the work sequencing process unlocks it.For example, assume that outbound work sequencing is enabled, the work release sequencing type on the outbound load is by stop, and movement paths for case pick and each pick locations among other hops (like Print/Wrapper stations) include a pre-stage movement zone. Assume also that movement paths for pallet picks have other hops (like Print/Wrapper stations) but not a pre-staging hop. During allocation, pick work for the load is created in the work queue. Case pick or Each pick work having a pre-stage movement zone defined as a hop in the movement path are not locked (ignoring any outbound work sequence). However, subsequent work out of the pre-staging hop to the staging destination is locked. Pallet pick work is locked at source zones and will be unlocked along with any locked transfers out of pre-stage by outbound work sequence only after all the cases and eaches are pre staged. When the first stop is completely staged, then pick and transfer work for stop 2 is unlocked for delivery to staging; and so on.Note: If a movement path contains pre-stage zones, the application does not override the initial status of work created for an operation. For example, if an operation is configured to be created with an initial status of Locked and pre-staging is used, the work to pick inventory to the pre-stage zone remains in a locked status until manually unlocked. Therefore, to ensure that work is available for operators to complete prior to pre-staging, the Initial Creation Status field for the operation should be set to Pending. This field is only available if outbound work sequencing is enabled. See Outbound work sequencing.If No, then this movement zone is not used for pre-staging.
Identifier or name of the criteria definition.
Meaningful description for the criteria. The description assists the user in identifying the criteria when they assign it to a hop.
Operation that creates work to move inventory out of the zone.
Priority at which the work is added to work queue. If you leave this field blank, then the base priority defined for the operation is used.
Unique identifier for a movement path. A movement path specifies the path that inventory takes from one point to another through your facility.
Movement zone that contains the location from which inventory is initially picked or moved. It represents the first movement zone on the movement path.

Movement zone that contains the final destination location for inventory that was picked or moved. For example, for inventory picked for an outbound order, this could be a zone that contains ship staging locations.

LPN level of inventory to which the movement path applies.• LPN: Typically represents a pallet.• Sub-LPN: Typically represents a case.• Detail LPN: Typically represents an each or piece. The units of measure (UOMs) associated with LPN, sub-LPN, and detail LPN levels are defined by the System Equivalent UOM field in the item footprint. See Item Footprint UOM fields.
If Yes, the details of a hold are automatically displayed when the RF operator scans inventory that is on hold.If No, hold details are not automatically displayed.

If Yes, then when a lot number is entered during receiving, the application retrieves the manufactured or expiration date embedded in the lot number. For example, when an operator receives lot-tracked inventory and enters the lot number for an item, the application analyzes the lot number and populates the manufactured date and expiration date (as applicable) from the information embedded in the lot number. If this field is set to Yes, then lot parsing only takes place if the lot number is based on a valid lot format (assigned to the item) that is configured for date parsing.If No, the application does not parse dates from lot numbers.

If Yes, then an operator that is performing a pick or count can recover inventory that the application shows (logically) as being in a lost location. The recovery process prompts the operator to confirm the contents of the LPN with what the application expects. If the content matches, the operator can update the location of the inventory to its current physical location and then continue with the pick or the count. If the content does not match, the location of the inventory cannot be updated to the current location.If No, then for an inventory discrepancy during a pick, the application is typically configured to generate a count; for an inventory discrepancy during a count, the application is typically configured to generate an audit count.

If Yes, then an operator that is performing a pick or count can recover inventory that the application shows as being in a different physical location than where the pick or count is taking place. The recovery process prompts the operator to confirm the contents of the LPN with what the application expects. If the content matches, the operator can update the location of the inventory to its current physical location and then continue with the pick or the count.If No, then for an inventory discrepancy during a pick, the application is typically configured to generate a count for both the current location and the physical location of the inventory; for an inventory discrepancy during a count, the application is typically configured to generate an audit count.

If Yes, the RF operator is presented with an inventory summary display when the operator performs an inventory query. You also select the inventory attributes by which the display of inventory in a location is grouped (summarized).When the RF operator performs an inventory query, the Inventory Query screen lets the operator enter selection criteria, and flow to the next screen. If the Inventory Summary Display screen is enabled, then the Inventory Summary Display screen is displayed and shows the quantity of inventory in each location summarized by the fields configured for display. For example, if Lot Number is assigned to be displayed, the screen displays a record that shows the item and item client (for a 3PL environment), and the quantity of inventory in a location that has the same lot number. The next record shows the quantity of inventory for the next lot, and so on. Following the inventory summary of the last record, the Inventory Display screen is displayed showing inventory details.If No, the Inventory Summary Display screen is not display; instead, the Inventory Display screen shows the storage location, item, and all of the inventory details for one record.In both instances, a page number on the RF screen indicates how many records were retrieved matching the selection criteria that was entered. The operator can scroll through the records, or page back and forth between records.

Minimum number of characters that the application accepts when an LPN is entered on a device or workstation during inbound identification and during picking. If the entered value falls outside of the range (for example, if a larger number is scanned into the LPN field), then the application does not accept that value. The Minimum Length and Maximum Length fields can be used to help prevent the application from accepting other values, such as a UPC or location, instead of an LPN.

Maximum number of characters that the application accepts when an LPN is entered on a device or workstation during inbound identification and during picking. If the entered value falls outside of the range (for example, if a larger number is scanned into the LPN field), then the application does not accept that value. The Minimum Length and Maximum Length fields can be used to help prevent the application from accepting other values, such as a UPC or location, instead of an LPN.

If Yes, RF operators are required to enter or scan either an item or location when performing a query on the RF Inventory Display screen.If No, the operator is still required to enter at least one value on the RF Inventory Display screen before performing a query. Regardless of whether this field is set to Yes or No, the maximum number of results that are displayed is dependent on the value in the Maximum Rows field.
Maximum number of rows displayed when an RF operator performs an inventory query.

Percentage of catch quantity below an item's defined minimum catch quantity that is deemed to be within tolerance. The application calculates catch quantity limits based on an item's configuration, but this value overrides the minimum tolerance and allows you to accept a lower value that would otherwise not be acceptable. For example, if an item's minimum catch quantity is 100, but the extreme minimum tolerance for a warehouse is 15 (15%), then whenever the warehouse captures catch quantity for the item, the application accepts a minimum value of 85.Note: In a 3PL environment, the client configuration for this field overrides the warehouse level configuration.

Percentage of catch quantity above an item's defined maximum catch quantity that is deemed to be within tolerance. The application calculates catch quantity limits based on an item's configuration, but this value overrides the maximum tolerance and allows you to accept a higher value that would otherwise not be acceptable. For example, if an item's maximum catch quantity is 100, but the extreme maximum tolerance for a warehouse is 15 (15%), then whenever the warehouse captures catch quantity for the item, the application accepts a maximum value of 115.Note: In a 3PL environment, the client configuration for this field overrides the warehouse level configuration.

If Yes, the application does not prompt the operator to recapture the catch quantity when the catch quantity of inventory is beyond its normal tolerance limits and within the extreme tolerance limits for the client. The application accepts the entered catch quantity for the inventory. For example, if an item's maximum catch quantity is 100, but the extreme maximum tolerance for the warehouse is 15 (15%), then whenever the application captures catch quantity for the item and warehouse within a value of 115, the application does not prompt the RF operator to recapture the catch quantity.If No, the application prompts the operator to recapture the catch quantity when the catch quantity of inventory is beyond its normal tolerance limits and within the extreme tolerance limits for the client.If the captured catch quantity is beyond the minimum or maximum extreme tolerance limit, the application does not allow the operator to proceed further and prompts the operator to recapture the catch quantity irrespective of the value of Suppress Out of Tolerance Prompt.Note: In a 3PL environment, the client configuration for this field overrides the warehouse level configuration.

If Yes, the application does not prompt the operator to capture catch quantity at picking. Instead, the application requires the operator to capture catch quantity before loading. The application does not allow an operator to load inventory if the catch quantity is required but has not been captured. If you set this field to Yes, an operator can capture the catch quantity for an LPN or sub-LPN using directed or undirected work, depending on the following configurations:• If the Require Sub-LPN Capture field is Yes, and if catch-tracked inventory is deposited to a location type with the Create Sub-LPN Catch Work on Deposit field set to Yes, then the application creates directed work for the capture. If the inventory is not deposited to a location type enabled for creating directed capture work, then an operator must capture catch quantity using the undirected RF menu option. • If the Require Sub-LPN Capture field is No, then the option to create directed capture work upon deposit is disabled, and an operator must capture the capture catch quantity using the undirected RF menu option before loading. If No, the application prompts the operator to capture the catch quantity of inventory when picking a full or partial pallet.Note: In a 3PL environment, the client configuration for this field overrides the warehouse level configuration.

If Yes, the operator is required to capture the catch quantity of each sub-LPN during shipping (while picking or before loading). If you set this field to Yes, the point at which the operator captures the sub-LPN catch quantity depends on whether delayed capture is enabled (Delay Capture Until Loading field).Note: If a work assignment is picked to a sub-LPN, the individual case information (including catch quantity) is no longer retained. Therefore, the application does not prompt for sub-LPN capture if a work assignment is picked to a sub-LPN, even if this field is set to Yes. See Work assignments picked to sub-LPNs.If No, the operator is not required to capture the catch quantity of each sub-LPN during shipping; however, LPN catch quantity may still be required.Note: In a 3PL environment, the client configuration for this field overrides the warehouse level configuration.

If Yes, then when prompted to capture the catch quantity of inventory either during picking or before loading, the operator can cancel the capture request. If an operator cancels the catch quantity capture for an LPN or for a sub-LPN on an LPN, then the application will not prompt for a capture of the LPN again.If No, then the operator is required to capture the catch quantity of inventory when prompted by the application; the operator cannot cancel the prompt.Note: In a 3PL environment, the client configuration for this field overrides the warehouse level configuration.

If Yes, the application requires an approval, such as from a supervisor, for inventory that is outside of its normal tolerance but within the defined extreme tolerance limits. Inventory that is outside its normal tolerance but within the extreme limits is displayed with the Tolerance tag and must be approved (or adjusted) before it can be loaded and shipped. The application calculates catch quantity limits based on an item's configuration, and the values specified in Minimum Extreme Tolerance (%) or Maximum Extreme Tolerance (%). For example, if the minimum tolerance limit is 100, the minimum extreme tolerance limit is 85, and the captured catch quantity is 90, the application tags inventory as out of tolerance and prompts for a supervisor approval.If No, the application does not require an approval to ship inventory even if the catch quantity is outside the normal tolerance limits but within the configured extreme tolerance limits.Note: In a 3PL environment, the client configuration for this field overrides the warehouse level configuration.
If Yes, the user is required to provide a reason when performing or approving an adjustment.If No, the user does not need to enter a reason when performing or approving an adjustment.

If Yes, then when an item is assigned to a location and a different item is added to the location through an inventory adjustment, the application sets the location to Error status. An item is assigned to a location through a location preference rule, which prevents the application from directing other items to the location for putaway.If No, then when an item is added to a location through an inventory adjustment, the application does not consider the location's assigned item when it resets the location's status after an adjustment. If you set this field to No, it is possible for an item other than the assigned item to be added to a location.

Determines when inventory adjustments are sent (played) to the host.• Send individually: Adjustments are sent to the host as they are completed.• Send when complete: Adjustments are sent to the host in one transaction when they are all completed.You use the Transactions page in the Inventory module to view adjustment sessions and send them to the host.
Monetary value of an inventory adjustment (increase or decrease) at or above which an approval is required. A value of 0 (zero) indicates that approval is not required for an inventory adjustment.
Number of units (in the stocking unit of measure) of an inventory adjustment (increase or decrease) at or above which an approval is required.
Name of a type of inventory count. The attributes of a count type determine how the application processes the count.
Description that further defines the count type.

Base count type that determines how the count behaves. For example, if the base count type is Cycle Count, then the application processes counts of this type as cycle counts. A base count type is a count type that is distributed with the standard product.When you add a new count type, you must associate it with a base count type. For example, if you want to create a new audit count type, you must select "Audit Count" as the base count type, so that the application processes counts of this type as audit counts.It is also important to select the appropriate value in the Operation Code field for the count type. The operation defines how count work is added to the work queue, the priority of the work, and which users and equipment are authorized to perform it. For example, the Cycle Count operation is typically assigned to the cycle count types, so that cycle count work is added to the work queue. In the same way, the Count Audit operation is typically assigned to the audit count types. The operation code assigned to a new count type should match the operation code assigned to the count type selected as the base count type.

Work operation that the application uses when creating count work. The operation defines how count work is added to the work queue, the priority of the work, and which users and equipment are authorized to perform it.Note: The operation defined for the count type does not apply to count by LPN counts, which may be enabled for the count type. To defined the operation for count by LPN counts, see Configure count settings.For example, the Cycle Count operation is typically assigned to the cycle count types, so that cycle count work is added to the work queue. In the same way, the Count Audit operation is typically assigned to the audit count types. The operation code assigned to a new count type should match the operation code assigned to the count type selected in the Base Count Type field.

Type of count that is generated if a secondary count (such as a recount or audit count) is required. A secondary count is required if a discrepancy occurs during counting, and the End Location Count field is set to "Generate New Count" or "Find match or Gen New Count".

Action that occurs when the count for a location is finished.• Check Threshold: If the count quantity matches the previous count or the application count, no action occurs. If it does not match, the application evaluates the count threshold for the item and warehouse to determine if the adjustment is made or if a new count is generated using the count type selected for Next Count Type. The count threshold defined for the item overrides the count threshold defined for the warehouse. For example, location LOC3 contains 850 RUBBERBANDS and the item threshold is set to 1000. If a count is performed and there are actually only 800 RUBBERBANDS in LOC3, the application would not generate another count but would adjust the location count to 800 (because the discrepancy is less than the threshold value). However, if the count is performed and there are actually 1200 RUBBERBANDS in LOC3, the application would generate a count based on the next count type to verify (audit) the location before creating the adjustment (because the discrepancy is more than the threshold value).Note: If the count is below the threshold but the application cannot complete the adjustment, the application does not display a notification of the failed adjustment, and a new count is not generated. An adjustment may fail, for example, if the application requires homogeneous adjustments and the inventory is not homogeneous.• Find a Match: If the count quantity matches the previous count or the application count, no action occurs. If it does not match, then the location status is set to Inventory Error.• Find match or Gen New Count: If the count quantity matches the previous count or the application count, no action occurs. If it does not match, the application evaluates the count threshold for the item and warehouse to determine if the adjustment is made or if a new count is generated using the count type selected for Next Count Type. The count threshold defined for the item overrides the count threshold defined for the warehouse. If the count quantity is above the count threshold, then a new count is generated based on the Next Count Type value. If the count quantity is below the count threshold, then the adjustment is made, and a new count is not generated. Note: If the count is below the threshold but the application cannot complete the adjustment, the application does not display a notification of the failed adjustment; however, a new count is generated based on the Next Count Type. An adjustment may fail, for example, if the application requires homogeneous adjustments and the inventory is not homogeneous.• Generate New Count: A new count is generated.• Log Discrepancies: If the count quantity matches the previous count or the application count, no action occurs. If it does not match, the discrepancy is logged for future reporting but no additional action is performed.

Method that determines when the location being counted is restored to the status it was in before the count was released. When a count for a location is released, the location is locked until the selected release location method occurs.• Lock Down: The location is not released until the entire count is complete. Warehouses typically lock down a location when they use paper-based counting.• Standard: The location is released when the count for the location is complete. Warehouses typically use the Standard release when counting is performed using an RF device.

Specifies when to perform an adjustment.• Lock Down: Adjustments, if any, are performed when the entire count is complete.• Standard: Adjustments, if any, are performed when the count for the location is complete.

If Yes, the application automatically adjusts inventory when there is a count discrepancy during a summary count in a homogeneous location. A homogeneous location is a location that contains either a single LPN of one distinct item, or multiple LPNs of inventory, with each LPN containing a distinct item. Homogeneous locations must also contain inventory that either is not tracked by lot, revision, or origin code, or if tracked, has the same lot, revision, or origin codes for all of the inventory contained on an LPN. Inventory within homogeneous locations must not be sub-LPN or detail LPN tracked. In order for automatic adjustments to occur in homogeneous locations, the following conditions must be met:• The initial summary count must be configured to permit the same user who performed the summary count to perform the audit count.• The automatic adjustment must be less than the inventory adjustment cost and unit threshold defined for the item or warehouse. The thresholds defined for the item take precedence over the thresholds defined for the warehouse. The adjustment must be at or below both the cost and the unit threshold if both are defined.If No, the application does not automatically adjust inventory when there is a count discrepancy during a summary count in a homogeneous location.

If Yes, the counter must perform a detail count. A detail count requires the counter to enter each LPN and its quantity for a location. Select Yes if you want to ensure that each LPN in a location is counted.If No, the counter is prompted to enter the total quantity of inventory residing in the location. Select No if you are only interested in the total quantity in a location; not each LPN quantity.Note: For a configuration where the Base Count Type field is set to "Re-Count", if the Next Count Type field is set to "Audit Count", select No. If the Detail Count field is set to Yes, the application will not generate a detailed audit count after a detailed recount.

If Yes, then the following actions take place, depending on the type of count.• For a Summary count, if the quantity entered does not match the expected quantity, the user is prompted to re-enter the quantity. If the re-entered quantity does not match the expected quantity, the next action configured for the count type takes place.• For a Detail count:• If the user enters a quantity for an existing LPN that is different from the expected quantity, the user is prompted to re-enter the quantity until two consecutively entered values match. If the result is different from the expected quantity, then an inventory adjustment is performed automatically or sent for approval.• If the user enters a quantity for an LPN that does not exist in the location, the user is prompted to add the inventory to the system.If No, then the following actions take place, depending on the type of count:• For a Summary count, if the quantity entered does not match the expected quantity, the user is not prompted to re-enter the quantity. Instead, the next action configured for the count type takes place.• For a Detail count:• If the user enters a quantity for an existing LPN that is different from the expected quantity, then an inventory adjustment is performed automatically or sent for approval.• If the user enters a quantity for an LPN that does not exist in the location, the user is prompted to add the inventory to the system.

If Yes, then when an operator completes a detail count and there are unscanned (uncounted) LPNs in the count location, a warning message is displayed to confirm the removal of the unscanned LPNs from the location. For example, if the application shows that there are 5 LPNs in a location, but the operator only scans 4 LPNs during the detail count, then the application prompts the operator to confirm that the 5th LPN should be removed. If the operator confirms to remove the LPN, then the location inventory record is updated and the LPN is deleted. If the operator declines to remove the LPN, then the operator can scan the additional LPN that was missed before completing the count.If No, then the application does not prompt the operator to confirm the removal of unscanned LPNs during a detail count. When the count is completed, any unscanned LPNs are removed from the application.Note: This field is only available if the Detail Count field is set to Yes.

If Yes, the operator is directed to count empty locations. Select Yes if you want to verify that no unexpected inventory exists in locations that the application considers logically empty. This could happen, for example, if an operator moved inventory into a location without scanning the location,If No, the operator is not directed to count empty locations.

If Yes, the user who originally counted a location is not allowed to perform the secondary (audit) count for that location if an audit count is generated, even if the user is authorized to perform audit counts. The audit count must be performed by another authorized user. Select Yes if you want to prevent an operator that is authorized to perform both initial counts and secondary counts from performing both counts at the same location.If No, any authorized user may perform the audit count.

If Yes, then when an automatic inventory adjustment occurs, the RF operator performing the summary count that triggered the adjustment is prompted to enter a reason code for the adjustment. If a default reason code exists, then the default reason code is displayed, and the operator can either accept the default or select a new reason code.If No, then the operator is not prompted to enter a reason code after an automatic inventory adjustment.

If Yes, the count type will be considered as an ABC count. Use this count type whenever an ABC count should be performed. See Automated ABC counts.If No, the count type will be considered as a non-ABC count.

If Yes, during counting, the operator is required to enter the catch quantity (such as weight) as well as the unit quantity for inventory that is tracked by catch quantity. Select Yes if you store items that are tracked by catch quantity and you want these values verified during inventory counts. A catch quantity is a quantity that is represented in catch unit measurements, which are variable weights or sizes of inventory that may exist within the same material handling (stock keeping) unit.If No, during counting, the operator is not required to enter a catch quantity (such as weight) for inventory that is tracked by catch quantity.

Percentage of a catch quantity discrepancy that is allowed. If a cycle count for a location results in a discrepancy greater than this value between the expected and counted catch quantity, then an audit count is generated automatically. This value is used to prevent minimal (acceptable) discrepancies from generating audit counts.If a catch quantity discrepancy falls within the limit, then an automatic inventory adjustment takes place to update the expected catch quantity to the counter's catch quantity.

Attribute of a location that the operator must confirm when performing a cycle count at a location. You can enter up to three attributes, such as Verification Code (locvrc) or Aisle (aisle_id) to provide an additional level of verification that the operator is performing the count at the correct location.

Defines the information that is displayed to the operator or printed on the count sheet for counts that are generated for locations in which the storage zone is configured to allow single items. Only one item is allowed to be stored a single-item location; mixing of inventory (different items) is not allowed.• Enter Item & Quantity (Blind): The operator is directed to the location to count, but the expected item is not displayed to the operator or printed on count sheets. The operator enters the item and quantity in the location. Not showing the item to the counter may take more time but forces the operator to enter the item rather than accepting the displayed value as correct. If you select this option, you can also select one or both of the following options: • Do not show item if detail count: Indicates that for detail counts, the application does not display (or include on count sheets) the expected items in the location. A detail count requires the operator to scan an LPN in the location, and then enter the item and quantity on the LPN. If another LPN is in the same location, the operator scans the next LPN and enters the item and quantity; and so on.• Do not show item if summary count: Indicates that for summary counts, the application does not display (or include on count sheets) the expected items in the location. The summary count requires the operator to enter the item and the total quantity in the location. • Enter Quantity Only (Prompted): The operator is directed to the location to count, and the item in the location is displayed to the operator or printed on the count sheet. The operator confirms that the item is in the location and enters the quantity for each item that the application expects in the location. Showing the item to the counter may save time, but if there is a different item in the location, the operator enters 0 for the quantity and then has to enter the correct item with the quantity. Prompted is typically used in warehouses that do not have item barcodes to scan during counting. Note: Prompted means the application displays the item to the counter. Blind means no item displays and the counter must enter the item. The counter always has to enter the counted quantity no matter if prompted or blind is used.

Defines the information that is displayed to the operator or printed on the count sheet for counts that are generated for locations in which the storage zone is configured to allow mixed (different) items to be stored in a location in the zone.• Enter Item & Quantity (Blind): The operator is directed to the location to count, but the expected item is not displayed to the operator or printed on count sheets. The operator enters the item and quantity in the location. Not showing the item to the counter may take more time but forces the operator to enter the item rather than accepting the displayed value as correct. If you select this option, you can also select one or both of the following options: • Do not show item if detail count: Indicates that for detail counts, the application does not display (or include on count sheets) the expected items in the location. A detail count requires the operator to scan an LPN in the location, and then enter the item and quantity on the LPN. If another LPN is in the same location, the operator scans the next LPN and enters the item and quantity; and so on.• Do not show item if summary count: Indicates that for summary counts, the application does not display (or include on count sheets) the expected items in the location. The summary count requires the operator to enter the item and the total quantity in the location. • Enter Quantity Only (Prompted): The operator is directed to the location to count, and the item in the location is displayed to the operator or printed on the count sheet. The operator confirms that the item is in the location and enters the quantity for each item that the application expects in the location. Showing the item to the counter may save time, but if there is a different item in the location, the operator enters 0 for the quantity and then has to enter the correct item with the quantity. Prompted is typically used in warehouses that do not have item barcodes to scan during counting. Note: Prompted means the application displays the item to the counter. Blind means no item displays and the counter must enter the item. The counter always has to enter the counted quantity no matter if prompted or blind is used.

If Yes, then in storage zones configured for single-item storage, the application automatically completes the count when the operator indicates that a count is finished, typically by selecting Done. Select this option if you want to eliminate the need for counters to complete the count in the Complete Cycle Count screen.If No, then in single-item storage zones, when an operator indicates that a count is finished, the Complete Cycle Count screen is displayed, requiring the operator to confirm that the count is complete.

If Yes, the application uses the ABC counting configuration to automatically schedule cycle counts for inventory based on the ABC code assigned to an item, location, or client. You assign one of the ABC codes to the clients, items, and locations that you want to be counted on a regular basis. The application automatically schedules the counts based on the assigned ABC codes. The counts are displayed on the Counts page in the Inventory module.If No, the ABC counting configurations are not enabled, and the application does not attempt to schedule counts based on ABC codes, regardless of whether they are assigned to items, locations, and clients.

field: Initial Start Date for ABC Counts
description: Date on which the application should begin scheduling ABC counts, based on the configuration of the ABC codes and count days calendar. Enter a date or click the calendar to select a date from the display. When this initial date is set, you are not required to update it again at the beginning of a new cycle count period.

Determines the type of ABC counts that are scheduled on the selected count days.• By Item: When a cycle count is scheduled for an item, all count zones in which the item is stored are counted in the cycle count period based on the ABC frequency setting for the item.Note: If you select to count by item (or item and supplier), then the application may ignore the daily quota for counts. The daily quota is derived from the number of locations eligible for counting divided by the number of days in the count cycle. When an item exists across multiple locations, the application creates and releases as many counts as needed to complete the total item count across all locations on the same day. The application processes counting by item this way so that a complete and accurate count for an item does not span multiple days, and any discrepancies with the item can be resolved sooner. • By Item and Supplier: When a cycle count is scheduled for an item and supplier, all items are counted in the cycle count period based on the ABC frequency setting for the supplier.• By Location: When a cycle count is scheduled by location, counts are scheduled for every countable location in the warehouse, whether the location has inventory in it (based on the ABC frequency of the item) or the location is empty (based on the ABC frequency of the location). Select this option to ensure all locations are counted whether they have inventory in them or not. For example, if an operator moves inventory into a location without scanning the location barcode during the deposit, that the counter catches the inventory in the location during counting since the application considers this location empty.• By Client: When cycle counting is performed by client, then all count zone locations that contain the client's inventory are counted.

Number of count days within a count period. A count period is the number of days it takes to schedule all of the ABC counts that must be performed at least once per period. For example, if you define a count period as 30 days. Then if your A code must be counted 3 times per period, the application schedules A counts every 10 days. If your B code must be counted 2 times per period, the application schedules B counts every 15 days. If your C code must be counted once per period, the application schedules C counts every 30 days.

Minimum number of count days that are required in count period. This value limits the number count days that can be removed from a count cycle as a result of exceptions that are added to the configuration.

Determines how the application calculates a count period.• Countable: A count period consists of count days (defined under Count Days), except for any dates marked as exceptions (defined under Exceptions). For example, if you select Countable, and then select Monday through Friday as count days, then a 30-day count period represents 30 weekdays. • Calendar: A count period consists of every day in the week, regardless of the days on which counts actually take place (count days). For example, if you select Calendar, then a 30-day count period represents 30 days including Saturdays and Sundays, regardless of which count days are selected.

Days on which cycle counts are performed. This configuration is used in determining which days are included in a count period. For example, if you set Period Day Interpretation to Count Days, and then select Monday, Wednesday, and Friday as count days, then the days in a count period consist of only Mondays, Wednesdays, and Fridays.You use the Exceptions field to select the dates on which exceptions to the count days occur. For example, you can select as an exception a holiday that falls on a day of the week that is set as a count day.
Reserved for future use.

Number of times per count period that you want to count items or locations to which the ABC code has been assigned.Use the ABC codes in the following ways:• A code: Use for the items or locations that must be counted more frequently than other codes. • B code: Use for items and locations that must be counted less frequently than A codes, but more frequently than C codes.• C code: Use for items or locations that must be counted less frequently than other codes. A count period is defined by a number of count days or calendar days, depending on the configuration of the Period Day Interpretation field.

If Yes, then when a user enters paper-based count results at a workstation, the expected quantity for the item is populated as the count quantity on the Count Entry page. If this field is set to Yes, the user can quickly confirm the count quantity without having to manually enter the quantity. If there is a discrepancy between the counted quantity and the original quantity, the user can modify the value before completing the count.If No, then the expected quantity is not displayed on the Count Entry page, and the user must enter the item quantity from the count sheet.

Minimum number of hours that must elapse following a count near zero count before another count near zero count can be generated for the same location. This value is used to ensure that operators are not prompted to perform count near zero counts repeatedly for the same location. For example, in a location that contains fast-moving inventory, inventory levels can be depleted many times a day to below the count near zero thresholds.

If Yes, then Event Management sends an alert to users that are configured in Event Management to be notified of count backs for which a discrepancy has been logged. An alert is only sent if Event Management is integrated with Warehouse Management.If No, then Event Management does not send an alert when a discrepancy is logged as a result of a count back.
Unique identifier for the count zone.
Description that further defines the count zone.
Name of the building in which the zone resides.

If Yes, then cycle counts in the zone are performed on an RF device. RF cycle counts transition through statuses such as Generated, Scheduled, Released, and In Progress. The location being counted remains available for inventory processing (such as picking and putaway) while cycle counts are pending. This is because RF-based counts are performed against real-time information, and the quantity in the location when the count was generated is not relevant at the time the count is performed. If you set this field to Yes, then cycle counts in the zone must be performed on an RF device and are not visible on the Count Entry page.If No, then cycle counts performed in the zone are paper-based. Paper-based counts are generated in an In Progress status, and the location being counted is unavailable for inventory processing until the count is complete. This ensures that the quantity of inventory that was in the location when the count was generated is the same as when the operator performs the count. In the application, the Count in Progress tag is immediately applied to the location when the count is generated. If this field is set to No, then paper-based cycle counts in the zone must be manually entered and completed before the location being counted is available for processing.Note: If the Detail Count field for the count type is set to No, then paper-based cycle counts are displayed on the Count Entry page. If the Detail Count field is set to Yes, then paper-based counts are displayed on the Audit Count page.

If Yes, the application directs an RF operator to perform a cycle count immediately following a pick or inventory transfer in the count zone if inventory in a location drops below the Threshold Value. The picking operator, if authorized for the count near zero operation, is prompted to perform the count. If the picking operator is not authorized, then another operator performs the count. Select Yes if you want to ensure that the inventory level is accurate when it falls below a certain amount.Count near zero functionality can be enabled by item and by count zone. Therefore, a count near zero can be generated for a location if the count zone is enabled for it, even if the item in the location is not configured for count near zero. If you enable count near zero for an item and leave the Count Near Zero Amount blank (null), then the application defers to the count zone configuration.Alternatively, if both the item and count zone are enabled for count near zero and have different thresholds, the value defined for the item takes precedence. For example, assume an item's threshold (count near zero amount) is 20 units and a count zone's location threshold is 25 units. After a pick is complete, if the remaining quantity in the location is 22, then a count is not generated because the quantity did not fall below the item's threshold.If No, then the count zone is not enabled for count near zero. However, a count near zero can still be generated for a location in the count zone if the item in the location is enabled for count near zero and the inventory falls below the count threshold for the item.

Minimum unit quantity or percentage of a location's capacity that must remain after a pick or inventory transfer is complete for the application to bypass an immediate count. If the remaining inventory in the location is below the threshold value, the application prompts the operator to perform a count immediately after the pick or transfer. In the first field, enter the value for the unit quantity or percentage. In the second field, select one of the following values:• Unit Quantity: Indicates that the threshold value represents the stocking unit quantity of the item in the location.• Percentage: Indicates that the threshold value represents a percentage of the location's capacity.For example, if you set the threshold value to 20%, then when the inventory level falls below 20% of a location's capacity, the operator is prompted to perform an inline count following a pick or inventory transfer. If you set this field to zero (0), then a count is generated when the location is empty (remaining unit quantity or percentage of the location's capacity being used is 0).Only available when the Count Near Zero is enabled for the count zone.Note: If an item and a count zone are enabled for count near zero and have different thresholds, the value defined for the item takes precedence. For example, assume an item's threshold (count near zero amount) is 20 units and a count zone's location threshold is 25 units. After a pick is complete, if the remaining quantity in the location is 22, then a count is not generated because the quantity did not fall below the item's threshold.

Action the application performs for the release rule when a count is generated.• Produce Audit Sheet: The application generates an audit sheet for you to print. This action is recommended when you are configuring a Count Audit count type and you do not want to create directed work for the audit.• Produce Count Sheet: The application generates a count sheet for you to print. This action is recommended when you are configuring a Cycle Count count type and you do not want to create directed work for the cycle count.• Create Work: The application creates count work (defined by the operation code configured for the count type) and sends it to the work queue.

Command line argument used to further define the action you want the application to perform after releasing the count. Contact your Blue Yonder project team if you would like to define additional arguments for the release rule.

If Yes, the All Zones Priority field becomes available for you to define the base priority for the work that is released to the work queue for the count type associated with the release rule. The base priority is the priority at which work enters the work queue.If No, the application uses the base priority defined for the work operation associated with the count type for the release rule.This field is only used if the selected action creates directed work.

Value that determines the base priority in which work is released to the work queue. The value defined for All Zones Priority overrides the base priority defined for the work operation for the count type associated with the release rule. For example, if the Count Audit count type is configured to use the Count Audit operation, and that operation is configured with a base priority of 2, you can override that priority with a higher or lower priority, depending on how quickly you want the work to be completed.The priority you define applies to all count zones unless an exception is defined for a specific count zone.Only available when the Override Work Priority field is set to Yes.
Unique identifier for the count zone to which this override applies. A count zone is a method of grouping locations for an inventory count.

Action the application performs for the release rule when a count is generated.• Produce Audit Sheet: The application generates an audit sheet for you to print. This action is recommended when you are configuring a Count Audit count type and you do not want to create directed work for the audit.• Produce Count Sheet: The application generates a count sheet for you to print. This action is recommended when you are configuring a Cycle Count count type and you do not want to create directed work for the cycle count.• Create Work: The application creates count work (defined by the operation code configured for the count type) and sends it to the work queue.

Command line argument used to further define the action you want the application to perform after releasing the count. Contact your Blue Yonder project team if you would like to define additional arguments for the release rule.

If Yes, the Zone Override Priority field becomes available for you to define the base priority for work that is released to the work queue for the count type associated with the release rule. The base priority is the priority at which work enters the work queue.If No, the application uses the base priority defined for the work operation associated with the count type for the release rule.This field is only used if the selected action creates directed work.

Value that determines the base priority in which work is released to the work queue for work done in the specific count zone you define. The value defined for Zone Override Priority overrides the default base priority and, if defined, the override priority you defined for all count zones. For example, the Cycle Count count type is configured to use the Cycle Count operation, and the operation is configured with a base priority of 40. If you override that value with a priority of 30 for all zones and you define a priority of 10 for a count zone that contains each pick locations, then when a cycle count is generated, the counts in the zone that contains each pick locations will be counted before the cycle counts located in other zones.Only available when the Override Priority field is set to Yes.
Text that defines the configuration for this region. For example, you may configure one region to use directed work and another region for operators to manually select the tasks to perform.

Number that the operator speaks to select this region. A region is an identifier for a group of settings that take effect when a voice operator performs a counting function using the region code. (A region is not related to a physical location in the warehouse.)You can configure voice counting differently, by region, to accommodate situations that require different settings. For example, you can configure a region to use directed work, and specify the operations to use, and then configure another region that does not use directed work.

If Yes, then the application directs the operator to the location where the cycle count is to be completed. Even if you select Yes, the operator has the option to specify a count location by scanning or speaking the location to complete a manual count in directed mode.If No, then an operator that signs on to a counting function using this region must manually select the location at which to perform a count operation.

Name of the pick method. A pick method is a set of configuration options that define how replenishment work is created and released. A Pallet Replen is used to move full pallets to a defined pick location; a Case Replen is used to move cases to a defined pick location.
Text that further describes the pick method.

Name of a configuration that determines what occurs when a pick fails pre-validation. Pick pre-validation is a process that determines whether inventory is available in a location prior to displaying the pick to an operator. Using a pre-validation scheme can help prevent an operator from being directed to a location that either no longer contains available inventory for the pick or which is locked from picking.After you have created a pick pre-validation scheme, you must assign the scheme to a pick method for the type of pick to which it applies. Assigning a pre-validation scheme to a pick method determines how the application handles pre-validation for the each pick method.

If Yes, then picks that are allocated using the pick method can be built into work assignments. A work assignment is a picking process by which the application combines individual picks into a list (work assignment) that an operator can perform in one picking tour, moving from one pick location to another until the list is complete.If No, then picks are not added to work assignments.

If Yes, when an operator performs a replenishment pick generated using this pick method, the application prompts the operator with the specific sub-LPN to pick. If you select Yes, the application assigns specific sub-LPNs to the replenishment picks on the work assignment at the time the picks are performed. The application tracks the inventory for each completed pick on the replenishment work assignment and applies picked quantities across the assignment, if necessary. For example, if a single pick of a mixed-item case satisfies two replenishment picks on the work assignment, both picks are updated and considered complete.If No, the application does not prompt the operator with the specific sub-LPN to pick. If you select No, the operator is only prompted with location, item, and quantity information for a pick, and is not directed to pick a specific case.

If Yes, then for detail level replenishments using this pick method, the application can allocate a full mixed item sub-LPN to satisfy the detail-LPN picks.
