The application tracks the inventory by the LPN to which it is picked, and retains any individual case IDs and case-level serialization previously associated with the inventory. • Sub-LPN (Case): Work assignments created from this rule are picked to a sub-LPN. If selected, when an operator scans the To ID prior to starting a work assignment, the ID is processed as a sub-LPN (even if an LPN is scanned). The application tracks the inventory by the sub-LPN to which it is picked; however, individual case IDs are not retained, and case-level serialization is not tracked if multiple cases are picked to the sub-LPN. When an operator scans the physical sub-LPN as the To ID, the application automatically generates an LPN identifier to associate with the physical sub-LPN. Therefore, each work assignment (and its picked inventory) is associated with a unique sub-LPN (user defined) and a unique LPN (application defined). The application also tracks the sub handling unit type for each sub-LPN scanned as the To ID, if applicable. This is useful for work assignments that contain case or each picks being sent to the same customer.See Work assignments picked to sub-LPNs.Notes: • Carton picks are excluded from work assignments built with a rule configured to pick to the sub-LPN level. • If the Require Sub-LPN Capture inventory settings configuration is set to Yes for the warehouse or client (in a 3PL environment), then the application tracks the case identifier and respective catch quantity. However, if a work assignment is picked to a sub-LPN, the individual case information (including catch quantity) is no longer retained. Therefore, the application does not prompt for sub-LPN capture if a work assignment is picked to a sub-LPN.• Voice devices do not support tracking handling units. Therefore, when a voice operator picks a work assignment to an LPN or sub-LPN, the application does not track any associated handling unit or sub handling unit type.
Work operation that identifies the type of directed work that is created for the work assignment. Select an operation if you selected Create Work in the Release Action field.

field: Force to Pick Up Previous LPNs
description: If Yes, an operator who resumes an incomplete work assignment is directed to pick up the previously picked inventory. Select Yes to ensure that the remaining picks are picked to the original LPN.If No, an operator who resumes an incomplete work assignment is not directed to pick up the previously picked inventory.

If Yes, then during picking for a work assignment, the operator is notified when all of the picks in the current work zone are complete. Select Yes, for example, to notify the operator so that the operator can choose to deposit the work assignment to a pickup and deposit location where it can be picked up by another operator in the work zone of the next pick.If No, then the operator is not notified when the picks in the current work zone are complete.

If Yes, the application assigns a slot number to each pick that is generated by a slot work assignment rule. Select Yes for a master work assignment rule that is processed in conjunction with a slot work assignment rule. In this configuration, the two rules are added to a rule group so that the application processes the slot rule and then the master rule. With the Assign Slot field set to Yes for the master rule, the application assigns a slot number to each pick based on the slot rule from which it was processed.If handling unit types are specified for the work assignment rule, then picks are assigned slot numbers based upon one of the following configurations:• The handling unit type specified in the GROUP BREAK area of the slot work assignment rule • The handling unit types associated with the slots of the handling unit type specified in GROUP BREAK area for the master work assignment ruleTo assign slots without handling units, see Work assignment setup for picking to slots. To assign slots based on handling unit configurations, see Handling unit slots setup tasks.If No, the work assignment rule does not assign a slot number to each pick. Select No for work assignments that are not picked to slots, or for a slot work assignment rule that is processed with a master work assignment rule.

field: To Previous Operator After Inline Replenishment
description: If Yes, then if an operator sets down an incomplete work assignment to perform an in-line replenishment, the same operator is directed to resume the same work assignment upon completing the in-line replenishment. An in-line replenishment is a replenishment performed by a picking operator during a work assignment when the specified location does not have the pick quantity available. Select Yes to ensure that the operator who stops working on a work assignment to complete an in-line replenishment is also directed to resume the work assignment when the replenishment is complete.If No, then any authorized picking operator may resume the work assignment interrupted by an in-line replenishment.

If Yes, the application does not consolidate picks for the same item (same attributes and source location) during picking. If multiple orders contain picks for the same item, setting this field to Yes ensures that the application will not consolidate picks across multiple orders for the same work assignment.This configuration is useful for rules used to build work assignments for sequenced orders. Sequenced orders are used for picking and shipping inventory in the same item family set sequence for multiple orders in a sequenced fashion, typically in the order in which the items are required in a production line. For example, assume there are 4 each picks (2 for item A and 2 for item B) meant to be picked in alternating order (1A, 1B, 1A, 1B). If this field is set to Yes, the application directs the operator to pick the items in order sequence instead of consolidating the picks into 2 picks of 2 eaches (2A, 2B).Note: Preventing pick consolidation is especially useful if operators pick sequenced orders to non-slotted handling units. In this case, preventing pick consolidation retains the pick and deposit sequence of stacked items. However, if operators pick sequenced orders to slotted handling units, the deposit sequence is kept regardless of this configuration because each pick has an assigned slot. Since the deposit sequence to slotted handling units is enforced even if picks are grouped, preventing consolidation in this case may lead to increased travel time for pickers with no difference in the result.If No, the application does not prevent pick consolidation, meaning that multiple picks for the same item may be consolidated into a single pick.

field: Pick Tasks on Existing Work Assignments
description: If Yes, then the application can build new work assignments using pick tasks that are already built into an existing work assignment. For example, assume the application builds a new work assignment using a rule with this field set to Yes. If there are picks on existing work assignments that meet the rule criteria for the new assignment, the application removes the picks from the existing work assignment and adds them to the new work assignment.Note: When this field is set to Yes, any existing work assignment that has not been acknowledged may be downsized by the application, and possibly deleted altogether, if the removed picks were the last picks in the assignment. However, if all of the existing eligible picks to be removed are included in a trolley work assignment (picking to slots), the application does not remove them from the existing assignment.If No, then the application cannot remove picks on existing work assignments for new assignments.

field: Fill Work Assignment with Similar Picks First
description: Determines if and how the application prioritizes sorting similar picks to fill a single work assignment until a new work assignment is needed (based on the group break value for the rule).• Item Number: Picks are prioritized by item first, and then other defined sequence criteria are applied. For example, assume the criteria sequence for a rule is defined by pick zone first. If you select Items in this field, the application instead groups all of the picks for the same item first, and then sorts them by pick zone before adding them to the work assignment. • Order Number: Picks are prioritized by order first, and then other defined sequence criteria are applied. • No Selection (blank): The application does not attempt to fill work assignments with similar picks first.If you select a value for this field, and if the capacity for the current work assignment is reached, additional picks for the same item or order may be added to a new work assignment that includes picks for additional items or orders based on the selection criteria. However, the application attempts to ensure that the same item or order is only included in one split work assignment. For example, assume the value of this field is Items, and that Item A must be split across two work assignments due to capacity. One of the work assignments contains only picks for Item A, and the other includes the remaining picks for Item A and any other eligible picks that meet the selection criteria, if there is available capacity.If you select a value for this field and the Pick Tasks on Existing Work Assignments field is set to Yes, the application may split an item or order to more than one mixed work assignment in certain scenarios. It is recommended that if you select a value for this field, then the Pick Tasks on Existing Work Assignments field should be set to No to avoid unexpected behavior.Similarly, if you select a value for this field, then the Split Pick Tasks Across Assignments field should be set to No.It is also recommended that if you select a value for this field, the Assign Picks to Existing Assignment field should be set to Never to ensure that picks are not added to or removed from an existing work assignment that contains similar picks.

Determines whether and when the application is allowed to add picks to an existing work assignment.• Always: The application can assign picks to the work assignment at any time, including after acknowledgment, as long as the work assignment is not complete. • Before In Progress: The application can assign picks after the work assignment has been created, but not after an operator acknowledges (signs on to) the directed work to perform the work assignment. • Never: Prevents the application from assigning additional picks to an existing, generated work assignment, even during the first run of pick release.• Single: The application can only assign picks to the work assignment during the first run of pick release. For example, if a group of picks is released and List 1 is created using a rule with this field set to Single, then while the application is still evaluating the initial group of picks to build into additional work assignments, eligible picks can be added to List 1 until all picks in the group have been evaluated. If more picks are released, then the application does not consider assigning additional picks to List 1.

If Yes, then during the generation of work assignments, if a single pick exceeds the available capacity of a work assignment, the application splits the pick across two work assignments. For example, if a pick quantity is 10 but the work assignment capacity can only allow 3, then with this field set to Yes, a pick quantity of 3 is added to the first assignment and the pick for the remaining 7 is added to another work assignment. The application splits pick tasks based on the picking UOM to ensure that all split quantities are pickable.If this is set to Yes, then Fill Work Assignment with Similar Picks First must be blank to fill work assignments to maximum capacity. For example, if Fill Work Assignment with Similar Picks First is set to Orders, then new work assignments will be created for orders that exceed the capacity of the existing work assignment (leaving available capacity).If No, then if a pick exceeds the available capacity of a work assignment, the pick is not split and instead must be added as a single pick to a work assignment with available capacity for the original pick quantity.

Maximum number of starter pallets that can be included in a single work assignment. A starter pallet is a major quantity base pick that is used to begin a less than full pallet picking tour. Set this value to zero or blank if you do not want to limit the number of starter pallets in a work assignment. The value you specify here overrides the value set for the Maximum When Not Specified field on the work assignment.

Handling unit type that is required for work assignments generated using this rule. If you specify a handling unit type and also define group break values, the application uses the value that represents the lowest capacity. For example, if the handling unit type supports a maximum weight of 500, but you specify a group break value to be a maximum weight of 450, the application limits the work assignment to 450. If a handling unit type is specified on the order line, the application uses that handling unit type and does not assign the picks for that order line to a work assignment that uses a different handling unit type.

Maximum number of handling units that can be included in a work assignment created with the rule. If you select a value from the Handling Unit Type drop-down list, then the maximum number of handling units defines the capacity of the work assignment based on the maximum volume or weight (if lower than the break value) for the handling unit type.For example, if the handling unit type Pallet has a maximum volume of 10,000 cubic inches, and the maximum number of handling units per assignment for the rule is 2, then the maximum capacity of a work assignment is 20,000 cubic inches (2 x 10,000). However, if you specify a handling unit type and also define group break values, the application uses the value that represents the lowest capacity. Therefore, if the break value for the rule is 8 cubic feet (13,824 cubic inches), then the application uses the break value maximum for work assignments created with the rule because it is a lower capacity than the volume of 2 pallets (20,000 cubic inches). Alternatively, if the break value is greater than 20,000 cubic inches, then the handling unit capacity is used instead.Notes: • If you enter a value greater than 1, then the Assign Picks To Existing Assignment field should be set to Never. • When processing work assignments with multiple handling units, the application does not re-plan picks based on pick cancellations or skipped picks. For example, if a pick for the first handling unit is cancelled, the application would not move any picks destined for the second handling unit to the first handling unit. Similarly, if a pick is skipped on the first handling unit, the application will not move the skipped pick to the second handling unit. • Labels are only printed for handling units to which inventory has been picked. Labels are not printed for empty handling units.

If Enabled, the work assignment rule group is enabled for use. A work assignment rule group must be enabled to make it available for selection when creating work assignments either manually or automatically.If Disabled, the work assignment rule group is not available for selection when creating a work assignment.

Name of the work assignment rule group. A work assignment rule group is a set of work assignment rules that you want the application to run sequentially when creating work assignments based on the rule group.
Description that further defines the work assignment rule group.

Unique identifier for a client who houses inventory within a multi-client (third-party logistics) warehouse. The client identifier distinguishes one client from another so that the application can effectively manage inventory and activities for multiple clients in the same warehouse.

Attribute used to define the capacity of a work assignment.• Count: Defines capacity by the quantity of the attribute selected in the Group Break Field and Maximum Quantity fields. For example, you can restrict a work assignment to a single item or to a maximum number of cartons. • Volume: Defines capacity by a cubic volume, the values for which you enter in the Maximum Volume and Volume Threshold fields. You can also enter a value for Maximum Pick Weight to specify the maximum weight of picks that can be added to a work assignment after the volume threshold has been met. Volume calculations depend on the accuracy of item footprint information. • Weight: Defines capacity by weight, which you enter in the Maximum Weight field.• Pick Quantity: Defines capacity by the unit quantity, which you enter in the Maximum Pick Quantity field. See Work assignment rule break values.

Entity by which the capacity of a work assignment is determined, such as the maximum number of orders allowed. The value in the Maximum Quantity field determines how many can be included in a work assignment. For example, if this field is set to Items and the Maximum Quantity field is set to 5, then work assignments built using the work assignment rule cannot include more than 5 items. This field is only available if the Group Break Function field is set to Count.

Value that determines the maximum quantity for a work assignment; the Group Break Field value determines the entity for which the max quantity applies. For example, if the Group Break Field is set to Items and the value of this field is 5, then work assignments built using the work assignment rule cannot include more than 5 items. This field is only available when the Group Break Function field is set to Count.

Maximum cubic volume of inventory to include on a work assignment. The volume of the inventory is derived from the dimensions specified for the item footprint UOMs of the picked inventory. This field is only available if the Group Break Function field is set to Volume.Note: If you specify a handling unit type for the work assignment rule and also define group break values, the application uses the value that represents the lowest capacity. For example, if the selected handling unit type has a maximum of 5,000 cubic inches and the maximum volume break value is 5 cubic feet (8,640 cubic inches), then the application uses the handling unit type capacity instead of the break value maximum for work assignments created with the rule.

Minimum volume of inventory that is required to create a work assignment with the rule. The volume of the inventory is derived from the dimensions specified for the item footprint UOMs of the picked inventory. For example, you can set a higher minimum volume to exclude case picks but allow full layer picks. Only available if the Group Break Function field is set to Volume.

Value that defines the cubic volume of the work assignment, at or above which you want to restrict the weight of each subsequent pick added to the work assignment. The value by which subsequent picks are restricted is defined in the Maximum Pick Weight field. A volume threshold is used to avoid adding heavy picks to the end of a work assignment. This field is only available if the Group Break Function field is set to Volume.

Maximum weight of a pick that can be added to a work assignment after the value specified for Volume Threshold has been met. This field is used to limit the weight of picks that are added to the end of a work assignment. This field is only available if the Group Break Function field is set to Volume.

Maximum amount of weight allowed for a work assignment. The weight of the inventory is derived from the weight specified for the item footprint UOMs of the picked inventory. Only available if the Group Break Function field is set to Weight.Note: If you specify a handling unit type for the work assignment rule and also define group break value by weight, the application uses the value that represents the lowest capacity. For example, if the selected handling unit type has a maximum weight of 400 pounds and the maximum weight break value is 500 pounds, then the application uses the handling unit type capacity instead of the break value maximum for work assignments created with the rule.

Minimum amount of inventory by weight that is required to create a work assignment with the rule. The weight of the inventory is derived from the weight specified for the item footprint UOMs of the picked inventory. Only available if the Group Break Function field is set to Weight.

Maximum unit quantity that is allowed for a work assignment. This value is typically used to limit a work assignment for a slot to the number of pieces that the slot can hold. Only available if the Group Break Function field is set to Pick Quantity.

Do not prompt user — Skip the pick — 5 — Cancel -reallocate — If pre-validation fails, the pick is skipped without notifying the operator. If pre-validation fails more than 5 times, the pick is cancelled.
Notify user — Cancel the pick — 0 — Cancel -reallocate — If pre-validation fails, the operator is notified, and then the pick is cancelled.

Confirm with user — Skip the pick — 2 — Cancel - reallocate — If pre-validation fails, the operator is notified and is asked to confirm the fail action. The operator can override the fail action and continue with the pick, or allow the application to skip the pick. Each time the pick fails pre-validation the operator must confirm the fail action. After 2 skipped picks, the pick is cancelled.
Disable Pre-Validation —  —  —  — Pre-validation is not performed. If the operator finds that inventory is not available in the location, the operator decides whether to skip or cancel the pick.
Unique identifier assigned to the pick pre-validation scheme.
Meaningful description of the pick pre-validation scheme.

Determines if pick pre-validation is enabled for the scheme and, if enabled, determines the processing that takes place when inventory cannot be picked from a pick location.• Disable Pre-Validation: The application does not determine whether pickable inventory is available in a location prior to displaying the pick to an operator.• Do not prompt user: When a pick fails pre-validation, the application does not display a message to the operator stating that a pick has been skipped or cancelled.• Notify user: When a pick fails pre-validation, the application displays a message to the operator stating that a pick has been skipped or cancelled.• Confirm with user: When a pick fails pre-validation, the application displays a message to the operator stating that the location does not have enough inventory to fulfill the pick, and asking the operator to confirm the fail action configured in the scheme. The operator can override the fail action if inventory becomes available and then continue with the pick, or allow the application to skip or cancel the pick according to the fail action defined for the scheme.

Determines if the application skips or cancels the pick when pre-validation fails or when there is insufficient inventory in the location to complete the pick.• Skip pick, use skip limit and cancel action: The application skips the pick and the pick is moved to the bottom of the work assignment.• Cancel pick: The application cancels the pick.Only available if pre-validation is enabled.

Determines the number of times a pick can be skipped before the application cancels it automatically. For example, if you enter 5, then after a pick is skipped 5 times, and the inventory is still not available the next time the application pre-validates the pick, the application cancels the pick. Only available when Skip pick is selected in the Fail Action field.
Cancel code configuration that determines how the application processes a cancelled pick. Only available if pre-validation is enabled. See Pick Cancellation.

Name of the pick method. A pick method is a set of configuration options that define how picks are created and released. You can create separate pick methods for outbound picks, which fulfill orders shipped from the warehouse, and for replenishment picks, which restock picking locations in the warehouse.
Text that further describes the pick method.

Name of a configuration that determines what occurs when a pick fails pre-validation. Pick pre-validation is a process that determines whether inventory is available in a location prior to displaying the pick to an operator. Using a pre-validation scheme can help prevent an operator from being directed to a location that either no longer contains available inventory for the pick or which is locked from picking.After you have created a pick pre-validation scheme, you must assign the scheme to a pick method for the type of pick to which it applies. Assigning a pre-validation scheme to a pick method determines how the application handles pre-validation for the each pick method.

Determines which locations in the movement zones defined for a movement path are reserved during pick release when the application uses this pick method.• All: During pick release, a location is reserved in all of the defined movement zones for a movement path. If selected, then the application only releases the picks if all zones in the movement path have an available location at the time of pick release; if not, the application does not release the picks until a location is available in all defined movement path zones.• First: Only the first deposit location (in the movement zone that follows the source zone) is reserved during pick release. Each subsequent location in the remaining movement path zones is only reserved when the operator picks up the inventory from its current location. If selected, and if there are no locations available in the first movement zone that follows the source zone, then the application does not release the picks. If a location is available and the picks release, but there is not a location available in the next zone in the movement path, then the operator can deposit the picks to a P&D location until a location is available in the next movement zone.• None: No locations in the movement zones defined for a movement path are reserved during pick release. The first deposit location (in the movement zone that follows the source zone) is reserved when the operator picks the inventory, and each subsequent location in the remaining movement path zones is only reserved when the operator picks up the inventory from its current location. If selected, the application always releases the picks, regardless of whether there are available locations in the movement path zones. If the next zone in the movement path is full, the operator can deposit the picks to a pickup and deposit (P&D) location until a location is available in the next movement zone.

If Yes, then picks that are allocated using the pick method can be built into work assignments. A work assignment is a picking process by which the application combines individual picks into a list (work assignment) that an operator can perform in one picking tour, moving from one pick location to another until the list is complete.If No, then picks are not added to work assignments.

If Yes, picks that are allocated using the pick method are subject to cartonization. Cartonization is the process of determining which items are to be packed together in a container and which size container is to be used.If No, picks are not cartonized.

If Yes, an operator completing picks that were allocated using the pick method is allowed to perform an in-line replenishment. An in-line replenishment is a replenishment performed by a picking operator when the specified location does not have the pick quantity available. For example, if an operator arrives at a location to complete picks and there is not enough inventory available, the operator can set down the completed pick work and immediately complete a replenishment to the location.If No, the operator is not directed to perform in-line replenishments when performing picks.

Movement zone that contains the final destination location for inventory that was picked. For example, for inventory picked for an outbound order, this could be a zone that contains ship staging locations.

Action that the application performs to release the pick:• CREATE DIRECTED WORK: Creates a directed work request for the pick, which is added to the work queue so that an RF operator can perform it.• CREATE PICKS: Releases the pick as undirected work.• CREATE WORK FOR PM PRE MANIFEST PACKAGE: Creates a work queue entry for a case pick or kit pick, and manifests the parcel package. • PROCESS PM PRE MANIFEST PACKAGE: Creates a work queue entry for a case pick or kit pick, manifests the parcel package, and prints a manifest label with pick information and parcel package information.• CREATE LABEL FILE FOR PM PREMANIFEST PACKAGE: Manifests the parcel package and prints a manifest label with pick information and parcel package information.• PRODUCE PICK LIST: Produces a report that displays the pick information. An operator uses the report to perform paper-based picking. • PRODUCE SHIPMENT LABEL: Prints a pick label that includes the information for the pick work.
Work operation that identifies the type of work that is created, such as piece pick, case pick, kit pick, list pick, pallet pick, or replenishment pick.

Priority at which work initially enters the work queue. It is the priority at which a work request is created. Priority is used, for example, to assign a higher priority to pallet and case replenishment work to fill pick locations than to pallet or case pick work to fulfill orders.• Use base priority: The value for the operation's base priority at the time of allocation is used when work is created. The base priority is the current priority that is defined for the operation.• Override base priority: The operation's base priority is overridden at the time of allocation for the selected zone with the number specified in the Value field. For example, you may consider your case replenishments coming out of your flow racks more important than your case replenishments coming out of your floor zone.• Increase priority from base priority: The operation's base priority is increased at the time of allocation by the number specified in the Value field.• Decrease priority from base priority: The operation's base priority is decreased at the time of allocation by the number specified in the Value field.

Value that is applied against the base priority of the operation. Depending on what is selected for Priority, the value either replaces the base priority, or it is added to or subtracted from the base priority to result in a new priority.

If Yes, the operator is directed to confirm the quantity that was actually picked for a threshold pick. A threshold pick is an overpick performed by picking a higher UOM (such as a pallet) instead of multiple lower UOMs (such as cases) when the quantity required is slightly less than the higher UOM. (The threshold percentage that defines when a threshold pick can be performed is specified on the item footprint UOM.) For example, when an order line requires slightly less than a full pallet, the operator is directed to pick a full pallet rather than multiple cases; the quantity not needed for the order line is removed from the full pallet to be returned to storage.If No, the operator is not prompted to confirm actual picked quantities for a threshold pick.Note: It is recommended that the Confirmation for Threshold Pick field be set to Yes so that the application is notified that a quantity different from the required quantity was picked.

If Yes, then the application displays to the operator the item attributes (such as lot, revision level, and origin) in the location, if they are known and if the inventory is tracked by these attributes. When this field is set to Yes, the application populates attribute values that must be verified so the operator does not have to enter the information. The following pick verification configurations can affect whether and how attributes are displayed:• If pick verification for the attribute is required (either by default or when the pick verification override is set to Always), then the item attribute value is displayed prior to verifying the pick. If the pick location contains inventory with multiple values for an attribute, the application displays "Many" as the field value. The operator then verifies the specific attribute value of the picked inventory in a second field for the attribute, separate from the display field that is populated with the value (Many). • If pick verification for the attribute is not required, then the item attribute field is displayed without a value. If No, then if the item is tracked by certain attributes and pick verification is required, the operator must enter the attribute values in the pick fields. If verification is not required, then the item attribute fields are not displayed.

If Yes, the operator can enter the pick information and the destination LPN or location on a single RF screen. Selecting Yes may increase the speed at which the task is performed but may also increase the risk of an inaccurate entry for the destination because the operator must enter it during pickup.If No, the operator is prompted for the destination LPN or location on a second RF screen. Selecting No may reduce the speed at which the task is performed but may also increase the accuracy of the destination entry because the operator receives a separate prompt after completing the pickup.

Name of a pick zone. A pick zone represents a group of locations that share the same attributes for picking, such as the LPN level at which picks can be allocated, the cartonization group to which it belongs, and whether the location supports replacement picks and pre-inventory allocation. The search path searches pick zones when attempting to find inventory for allocation.
Category used to group menu options for the purpose of maintaining user authorizations. Roles are assigned to the appropriate user accounts to control the tasks users are authorized to perform.

Name of an order type. An order type is a category that is used to group orders based on the warehouse processing necessary to fulfill the order. For example, customer orders and distribution orders require different processing by the application, and so an order type can be assigned to categorize each order separately. The application uses order types, for example, to identify orders that are eligible for bulk picking, or to direct orders to specific destination locations.

Type of pick work to which the verification override applies.• Bulk Pick: Work type used to perform bulk picks.• Demand Replenishment: Replenishment work type generated when pre-inventory allocation is enabled and a pick location does not have inventory to complete an order. The application generates demand-based replenishments from reserve storage locations to the pick locations, and then generates picks based on the inventory pending to the pick locations.• Emergency Replenishment: Replenishment work type generated automatically when there is insufficient inventory in a pick zone to satisfy a shipment line.• Kit: Work type used to pick component items to fill a work order.• Manual Replenishment: Replenishment work type initiated by an operator for a specific location.• Pick: Work type used to pick inventory to fill an order.• Replenishment: Work type used to fill a pickface location with inventory from a storage location.• Stage Transfer: Pick work generated to transfer inventory typically from a cross docking location to a staging lane.• Top-off Replenishment: Replenishment work type generated automatically at timed intervals.• Triggered Replenishment: Replenishment work type generated automatically when an item in a zone or a location has dropped below a user-defined level.
Packaging level to which the override applies:• Detail LPN: Applies to each (piece) picks. • LPN: Applies to pallet picks.• Sub-LPN: Applies to case picks.

Name of a pick zone. A pick zone represents a group of locations that share the same attributes for picking, such as the LPN level at which picks can be allocated, the cartonization group to which it belongs, and whether the location supports replacement picks and pre-inventory allocation. The search path searches pick zones when attempting to find inventory for allocation.
Category used to group menu options for the purpose of maintaining user authorizations. Roles are assigned to the appropriate user accounts to control the tasks users are authorized to perform.

Name of an order type. An order type is a category that is used to group orders based on the warehouse processing necessary to fulfill the order. For example, customer orders and distribution orders require different processing by the application, and so an order type can be assigned to categorize each order separately. The application uses order types, for example, to identify orders that are eligible for bulk picking, or to direct orders to specific destination locations.

Type of pick work to which the deduction sequence applies.• Bulk Pick: Work type used to perform bulk picks.• Demand Replenishment: Replenishment work type generated when pre-inventory allocation is enabled and a pick location does not have inventory to complete an order. The application generates demand-based replenishments from reserve storage locations to the pick locations, and then generates picks based on the inventory pending to the pick locations.• Emergency Replenishment: Replenishment work type generated automatically when there is insufficient inventory in a pick zone to satisfy a shipment line.• Kit: Work type used to pick component items to fill a work order.• Manual Replenishment: Replenishment work type initiated by an operator for a specific location.• Pick: Work type used to pick inventory to fill an order.• Replenishment: Work type used to fill a pickface location with inventory from a storage location.• Stage Transfer: Pick work generated to transfer inventory typically from a cross docking location to a staging lane.• Top Off Replenishment: Replenishment work type generated automatically at timed intervals.• Triggered Replenishment: Replenishment work type generated automatically when an item in a zone or a location has dropped below a user-defined level.
Packaging level to which the deduction sequence applies:• Detail LPN: Applies to each (piece) picks.• LPN: Applies to pallet picks.• Sub-LPN: Applies to case picks.

field: Prompt for Barcode at Pick Confirmation
description: If Yes, then when a user opens the Pick Confirmation page to manually confirm picks, the application prompts the user to scan or enter a barcode to specify the picks to confirm. However, the operator is not required to enter a value to proceed. The barcode value can be a carton number, a work assignment, or a work reference. If set to Yes, then after a barcode is entered, the Confirm Picks window is displayed and populated with the pick information.If No, then when a user opens the Pick Confirmation page, the application does not prompt the user to scan or enter a barcode. The user can either enter search criteria or select a quick filter to view pick information, or manually display the prompt to scan a barcode.

field: User Chooses Next LPN to Deposit
description: If Yes, after picking, the operator is allowed to either accept the displayed LPN to deposit or enter a different one.If No, the operator must deposit the displayed LPN.

field: Confirm Sub UCC Label at Picking
description: If Yes, when the operator picks a case that requires a UCC-128 label, the operator must confirm (scan) the label number and apply the label to the case during the pick. UCC-128 numbers are used to identify the contents of a case, and to send out advanced shipment notifications (ASNs) to external applications. Prior to beginning a picking tour, the application verifies whether there are picks that require a UCC-128 label; if so, the operator can print the labels and begin picking. When the operator picks a case that requires a label, the RF Subucc Confirmation screen is displayed, and the operator must scan the UCC-128 label to confirm the label is valid for the picked case. This confirmation is valid for outbound orders or replenishments that require cases and are picked individually or as part of a pick list.If No, the operator can still print the UCC-128 labels prior to picking, but the application does not validate whether the correct label is applied to a case.

If Yes, the Order Details Display screen is accessible to the operator during picking. The order details information includes the customer, order, item, carrier, shipment, stop, and load for which the pick is required. If notes exist on the order, the order information is displayed before the notes are displayed.If No, the Order Details Display screen is not accessible to the operator. However, if available, the operator can still view order notes.

Determines the point during outbound order processing when the Load Preparation screen is displayed to the operator. The Load Preparation screen displays the handling unit type and LPN attributes that must be applied to the inventory before it is loaded onto transport equipment.• Deposit: Displays the screen after a selection is made on the Product Deposit screen.• Picking: Displays the screen during a pick after the item has been confirmed.• Picking and Deposit: Displays the screen after each pick is completed and after a selection is made on the Product Deposit screen.
If Yes, then UCC-128 processing is enabled.If No, then UCC-128 processing is not enabled.

If Yes, then each pick work entry for a sub-level UCC-128 label will be generated with a different cmbcod, allowing the picks to be confirmed individually.If No, then all pick work for a sub-level UCC-128 label will be generated with the same cmbcod, allowing the picks to be confirmed in one batch.

If Yes, then Secure Voice functionality is enabled for voice picking. Secure Voice provides an encrypted communication method in which the device and the application server communicate through encrypted JSON messages over API web calls using an https (secure) socket. With Secure Voice enabled, the application server can communicate with the voice device over a public network and does not require the use of a VPN tunnel or Integrator processing. Additionally, Secure Voice ensures user authentication happens first in the voice device's start-up sequence, meaning that subsequent messages are only sent to authorized users. Re-authentication occurs when required, such as when an authorization token expires or is manually revoked.IMPORTANT: Secure Voice requires additional server and device configuration. If Secure Voice is enabled, then the voice device must be operating on a recently released firmware version with an up-to-date root certificate to properly validate the certificate used in the HTTPS connection. Before you enable Secure Voice, contact the Blue Yonder Edge team for assistance.If No, then Secure Voice is disabled, and the application communicates with the voice device through plain text CSV socked-based LUT/ODR messages (Integrator transactions).

If Yes, then when the device repeats the operator's password, the operator must confirm the password to continue. If the password is correct, the operator speaks "yes" to continue; if the password needs to be reentered, the operator speaks "no".If No, then the password is used without confirmation from the operator. If the password is correct, the operator is logged in. If the password is incorrect the operator is instructed that the password is incorrect and is required to speak the password again.Note: MCL Voice does not support this configuration.

If Yes, a description for the item being picked is always spoken to the operator.If No, the device does not speak the item description unless there is more than one item in the pick location or the operator requests it by speaking "description".

Determines how the picking operator should be prompted for location and quantity during voice picking.Note: MCL Voice only supports the Multiple - Location, item and quantity selection for this configuration.• Single - Location, item, and quantity: The device prompts the operator with the pick location, item information, and quantity at the same time with no need for confirmation.• Single - Location, item, and quantity (Suppress Quantity: 1): The device prompts the operator with the pick location, item information, and quantity at the same time. However, if the pick quantity is 1, the device only gives the pick location and item information; that is, if the device does not specify a pick quantity to the operator, the pick quantity is 1. This is useful for facilities that regularly voice pick quantities of 1 because picking can be completed faster without the quantity prompt. • Multiple - Location, item and quantity: The device prompts the operator with the pick location and, in order to continue, the operator must respond with the voice check digit to confirm the location. After a location is confirmed, the operator is then prompted with the item information and pick quantity. This is the slowest prompt method, but it is useful when an operator needs to travel a long distance between picks and still recall the pick location. Note: If the Check Digit Rotation field is set to Yes, before an operator starts an assignment, the application specifies which of the three check digit values is required for pick and deposit locations.

If Yes, the device prompts the operator to provide the first (primary) check digit for a starting location, which is used to determine the best work to give to the operator.If No, the operator is not prompted for a starting location, which can streamline the login process, and the application uses the location specified in the Default Start Location field.

If Yes, then the operator is required to the speak the pick quantity for verification. For example, if the pick is for 5 cases, the following interaction would take place:• Device: "Pick 5 Case"• Operator: "Five"Note: The operator can speak less than the required quantity to create a short.If No, then the operator is not required to speak the pick quantity and instead must speak "ready" to confirm the full quantity. For example, if the pick is for 5 cases, the following interaction would take place:• Device: "Pick 5 Case"• Operator: "Ready"Note: MCL Voice does not support this configuration.

Location that is used as the default start location for a voice operator during the login process. This field is only available and is required if the Starting Location field is set to No. The application uses the start location as a determining factor when locating directed work for the operator.

If Yes, the operator only receives a pick quantity for what is available in a pick location. For example, if the pick is for a quantity of 10, but the location has only 5 available, then the operator is directed to pick 5. If the Auto Skip Picks field is set to Yes, then the remaining 5 are automatically skipped, and the operator is directed to perform the skipped picks after completing the other picks in the assignment.If No, the operator is instructed to pick the entire pick quantity. When the operator confirms a quantity less than the full pick quantity, the operator is instructed to pick the remaining quantity. The operator can then skip or cancel the pick for the remaining quantity.

If Yes, then when the operator requests a new container, the device directs the operator to deliver all closed containers before it allows the operator to open a new container. This option applies to cluster, bulk cluster, and non-carton work assignment picks when a container becomes full and the operator attempts to open a new container to complete the rest of the picks.If No, then the device does not direct the operator to deliver the closed containers when a new container is requested.

If Yes, the application selects randomly between three defined check digits (rather than one) when prompting an operator to confirm a pick or deposit location during voice picking operations. A check digit is a number assigned to a location that a voice operator speaks to confirm the location.By default, the three check digit fields for a location are titled First (Primary), Middle, and Last. If check digit rotation is enabled and voice pick configuration requires a location check digit, then when an operator starts an assignment, the application specifies which of the three check digit values is required for pick and deposit locations. For example, the voice device might speak "Middle," meaning the operator must use the middle check digit value to confirm each pick and deposit location for the assignment. When the assignment is complete, the application again randomly selects a check digit for the next assignment.You can change the description that is spoken to voice operators for each check digit field using the Voice Check Digit Schemes configuration.Note: Check digit rotation is only used during picking operations. During other voice operations that require check digit confirmation, such as replenishments, putaway, or distribution, the application always prompts for the first (primary) check digit.If No, then only the first (primary) check digit value is used to confirm locations when picking with a voice device in the current warehouse.

If Yes, then when the operator requests a new container, the application automatically generates a new container number and prints a label for it, and the device speaks the new container number to the operator.If No, then when the operator requests a new container, the device asks the operator to provide a container number. The value for the Print field determines whether and when a label is printed.

Number of characters, starting from the last character, that the voice device must speak to the operator to specify an LPN. This configuration is used to shorten the LPN value spoken to an operator that is depositing picked inventory, resuming a work assignment LPN, and loading transport equipment. For example, if LPNs in your facility typically consist of 8 characters, then to save time, you may require that the device speak only the last 4 characters of the LPN to the operator. If you set the value of this field to 4 and the LPN identifier is LPN01234, then when an operator deposits inventory, the device confirms the LPN by speaking the last four characters (1234). If you leave this field blank (no value), then the voice device speaks the full LPN.

If Yes, then after the operator has confirmed the catch weight values for a pick that requires it, the application prompts the operator with “Entries complete.” At this point, the operator can speak “Review last” to have the application repeat the last catch weight that was entered. Upon hearing the last entry, the operator can speak “Undo entry” and be prompted whether to undo the last entry, all entries, or continue. With this process, the operator can confirm or speak a different value for any of the catch weights that were captured.If No, then after the operator has confirmed the catch weight values for a pick that requires it, the application prompts the operator with the next location or the next piece of work. With this process, the operator does not have the option to review or change a catch weight value that has already been confirmed.

field: Assign Incomplete Work at Sign Off
description: If Yes, then when an operator that is picking a directed work assignment speaks "sign off," the application assigns the incomplete work assignment to the operator as if it were manually assigned. Set this field to Yes to prevent operators from signing off and signing on again to avoid the work they were originally directed to perform. If this field is set to Yes, then the incomplete work assignment remains assigned to the operator until one of the following events occurs: • The operator remains logged out for the duration that is specified in the Unassign Idle Work Time field.• The operator signs on to the application using a different device or vehicle type. • Warehouse Labor Management is integrated and the operator signs off for the entire day, meaning that the end of day transaction is sent to Warehouse Labor Management upon sign off (based on the End of Day field value).If No, then when an operator speaks "sign off," the directed work becomes available in the work queue for another operator to perform.Notes: • The application directs the operator to deposit incomplete work assignments based on the Deposit Incomplete Assignment on Sign Off field. • The Sign Off During Work Assignment field must be set to Yes to allow operators to sign off while performing a work assignment.

Number of minutes that work remains assigned to an operator after the operator has signed off. When the duration in minutes has passed, the work is unassigned and it becomes available for another operator to perform. Only available if the Assign Incomplete Work at Sign Off field is set to Yes.

Determines whether the application sends an end of day transaction (ISTOP or IEND) to Warehouse Labor Management when the voice operator signs out. Only available when Warehouse Labor Management is integrated with Warehouse Management.Note: The WLM Activity field in the Warehouse Labor Management integration fields determines which end of day transaction is sent.• Do not send, no prompt: The end of day prompt is not spoken to the operator, and the end of day transaction is not sent to Warehouse Labor Management when an operator signs off a voice device.• Always send, no prompt: The end of day prompt is not spoken to the operator, but the end of day transaction is always sent to Warehouse Labor Management when an operator signs off a voice device.• Labor check end of day: The system checks the Prompt for End of Day field in the Warehouse Labor Management integration configuration to determine if the application asks whether the operator is done for the day. If the operator is not prompted, the transaction is not sent. If the operator is prompted and the operator answers "Yes," then the transaction is sent.• Labor always prompt: A prompt asking if the operator is done for the day is always spoken regardless of how the Warehouse Labor Management Prompt for End of Day field is configured. This selection can be used to differentiate the prompt behavior for voice.

If Yes, the operator can speak "re-pick skips" to be directed to perform any picks in the current batch that were skipped. Picks skipped from a batch other than the one currently being picked cannot be re-picked using this command; instead, operators must wait until the application directs them to those picks again.If No, the operator cannot request to be directed to pick skipped picks at any time. Instead, the application directs the operator to perform skipped picks after completing the rest of the picks in the assignment.Note: MCL Voice does not support this configuration.

If Yes, the operator can speak "skip slot" to skip the current pick. The operator is directed to return to the location to complete the pick after completing the rest of the picks in the assignment.If No, the operator is not allowed to skip the current pick.

If Yes, the operator can use simple put verification when depositing picks into cartons. Simple put verification lets the operator speak the position number of the carton to verify the deposit instead of speaking the entire carton identifier. A carton's position number is established when the operator begins the assignment.If No, the operator must speak the carton number instead of the position number to verify the pick deposit.

If Yes, when a picking work assignment contains multiple cartons, each carton is tracked in a separate position on the destination picking equipment (such as a cart). The operator must confirm the position when depositing the picked inventory.If No, the operator is not required to confirm the carton or a position; the application records that the pick was placed into the proper carton.Note: MCL Voice does not support this configuration.

Determines the type of LPN to use for voice picking.• System-generated LPN: The application generates an LPN when the operator begins a picking assignment, and a label can be printed to apply it to the destination handling unit.• User-entered LPN: The operator enters the LPN from an existing label before beginning the assignment.

First field that the device speaks to direct the operator to pick up the correct inventory when resuming a work assignment. If you select a value for Override Resume Message First Field, the default message spoken by the device is overridden. Instead, the device speaks a resume message that includes the value of the defined first field followed by the value of the second field, if defined. For example, you can direct operators to resume a work assignment at an aisle location for a specific customer by selecting Ship-to Customer as the first field and Aisle as the second field, and the device would speak, "Pick up ship-to customer General Store, aisle A01." If you select no value (blank) in the override resume message fields, then the device speaks the default message that includes the LPN and location.Note: MCL Voice does not support this configuration.

If Yes, then the device spells the value of the first override field spoken to an operator that resumes a work assignment. Select Yes if the values for the selected first field typically include abbreviations not intended to be spoken as a word or phrase. For example, if the value of the ship-to customer is GS (General Store), with this field set to Yes, the device speaks each letter individually rather than speaking "GS" collectively as a word.If No, then the device does not spell the value of the first field in the override resume message. However, if the value includes numbers, then the device will speak each character in the field value individually.

Second field that the device speaks to direct the operator to pick up the correct inventory when resuming a work assignment. If you select a value for Override Resume Message Second Field, the default message spoken by the device is overridden. Instead, the device speaks a resume message that includes the value of the first field (if defined) followed by the value of the defined second field. For example, you can direct operators to resume a work assignment at an aisle location for a specific customer by selecting Ship-to Customer as the first field and Aisle as the second field, and the device would speak, "Pick up ship-to customer General Store, aisle A01." If you select no value (blank) in the override resume message fields, then the device speaks the default message that includes the LPN and location.Note: MCL Voice does not support this configuration.

If Yes, then the device spells the value of the second override field spoken to an operator that resumes a work assignment. Select Yes if the values for the selected second field typically include abbreviations not intended to be spoken as a word or phrase. For example, if the value of the ship-to customer is GS (General Store), with this field set to Yes, the device speaks each letter individually rather than speaking "GS" collectively as a word.If No, then the device does not spell the value of the second field in the override resume message. However, if the value includes numbers, then the device will speak each character in the field value individually.

If Yes, then a voice picking operator can sign on to multiple directed pick work assignments. For example, after an operator is prompted with a directed work assignment, the operator can add another work assignment by speaking "ready." Alternatively, the operator can speak "no more" to stop adding assignments and start picking.If enabled, the application combines the selected work assignments into a single master assignment, which allows the operator to efficiently complete the picks for multiple assignments at the same. Each work assignment is picked to its own separate container, and only one picking container can be open for each assignment at once.Note: The number of directed work assignments an operator can accept is defined by the LPN equipment limit specified for the operator's equipment. For example, if the LPN equipment limit is 3, then the operator can accept up to 3 work assignments. However, during multiple directed work assignment picking, the maximum number of LPNs is not enforced by the application; therefore, the operator is not prompted that the equipment is full or when to deposit LPNs.If No, then a voice operator can sign on to only one directed work assignment.

field: Confirm Work Assignment Pick by Position
description: If Yes, then during work assignment picking to multiple containers, the application assigns a position to the container and requires the operator to confirm the position before depositing the pick to it. Set this field to Yes if you allow the operator to speak a position instead of an LPN when depositing picks.If No, then during work assignment picking, the operator confirms the LPN to which the pick was deposited.Note: MCL Voice does not support this configuration.

If Yes, a voice operator is allowed to pick to multiple containers while picking a single work assignment. When the voice operator signs on to a work assignment and picks the first pick, the operator can speak "New container" to start another pick-to LPN. When this field is set to Yes, the first container remains open. In this way, the operator can add multiple containers and deposit picks for the work assignment by speaking the container position or LPN, depending on the setting of the Confirm Work Assignment Pick by Position field.In addition, when Allow Multiple Containers is set to Yes, the operator is allowed to partially pick an inventory quantity without shorting the remaining quantity to pick. For example, for a pick for 24 eaches, the operator can pick 12 and deposit the quantity to the first LPN, and then pick 12 more and deposit the quantity to the second LPN.If No, a work assignment must be picked to a single container. During work assignment picking, when an operator speaks "New container", the first container is automatically closed and a new container is opened for picking.Note: MCL Voice does not support this configuration.

Determines how the picking operator is prompted for the deposit location.• Confirm delivery location: The device prompts the operator with the delivery location and then waits for the operator to confirm by speaking the location check digits. Note: If the Check Digit Rotation field is set to Yes, the application specifies which of a location's three check digits is needed and prompts the operator for the defined value. • Confirm delivery location, 'Ready' allowed: The device prompts the operator with the delivery location and waits for the operator to confirm by speaking the location check digits. If the location does not have check digits, the operator can confirm the location by saying "ready".• Do not confirm delivery location: The device prompts the operator with the delivery location with no need for confirmation from the operator.• No delivery prompt: The device does not prompt the operator with the delivery location. However, if this option is selected, but printing container labels is enabled, then the device prompts with the delivery location.Note: MCL Voice does not support this configuration.

If Yes, the operator may take the picked inventory to the delivery location and speak "deliver now" to deposit picked items before all the picks for the assignment are complete.If No, the operator must complete all the picks before depositing them in the delivery location.

field: Deposit Incomplete Assignment on Sign Off
description: Determines where the application directs the operator to deposit inventory for incomplete work assignments when the operator signs off a voice device.• Prompt operator: The application asks the operator if the inventory should be staged. If the operator answers "Yes," then the application directs the incomplete work assignment to staging, and the remaining incomplete picks are added to a new work assignment. If the operator answers "No," then the application directs the work assignment to a pickup and deposit location, which keeps the assignment intact.• Staging: The application always directs the completed portion of the work assignment to a staging lane and the incomplete picks are added to a new work assignment (to split the work assignment). The remaining picks are returned to the work queue with the operation Work Assignment (LPCK). • Pickup and deposit: The application always directs the work assignment to a pickup and deposit location to keep the work assignment intact. The application updates the operation for the work assignment from Work Assignment (LPCK) to Resume Work Assignment (RLPCK).Note: This field is only valid if Deposit Prior to Completion is set to Yes.
If Yes, the operator can speak "cancel pick" to cancel the current pick.If No, operators are not allowed to cancel picks.

If Yes, the operator can speak "sign off" to sign off the device without completing the current assignment. However, if there is inventory on the device, the operator is prompted to deposit the inventory prior to being signed off. If labels are required for the picked inventory, they are printed prior to deposit.Note: The application does not require an operator to deposit inventory prior to sign off for cluster picking and bulk cluster picking; instead, the device prompts the operator to deposit the inventory when the operator signs on again.If No, the operator is not allowed to sign off the device prior to completing an assignment.

If Yes, when an operator that is picking a directed work assignment speaks "pass assignment" to deposit the inventory to a pickup and deposit location, the application unassigns the work from the operator. The application directs the operator to the pickup and deposit location in the same aisle in which the voice device is located. If there are multiple pickup and deposit locations for the aisle, or if one is not defined, then the application prompts the operator for the location. If set to Yes, the same or another voice operator can resume the work assignment through directed or undirected work.If No, then the work assignment remains assigned to the operator. Select No to ensure that operators are required to resume the assignments to which they were originally assigned.Notes: • If the Directed Multiple Work Assignments field is set to Yes, then when an operator speaks "pass assignment," completed work assignments are directed to staging, and the incomplete assignment is directed to a pickup and deposit location. • When an incomplete work assignment is set down, the application updates the operation for the work assignment from Work Assignment (LPCK) to Resume Work Assignment (RLPCK).

If Yes, the application speaks a summary of the pick assignment before directing the operator to the first pick. The summary provides values for each of the attributes that are selected to be included in the assignment summary, as defined by the Assignment Summary Attributes field.If No, the application does not provide a spoken summary of the assignment before directing the operator to the first pick.

If Yes, the application speaks a message, "Picks complete for zone," when all picks for the work zone have been completed and automatically deposits the carton in a pick and pass location (defined in the Deposit Location field). Select Yes if you want the application to determine when a carton is ready to be passed to the next operator in a pick-and-pass carton picking process.If No, the application does not inform the operator when picks are complete for the current work zone and does not automatically deposit the carton to the pick-and-pass location. Instead, the operator decides when to pass the carton to the next operator in a pick-and-pass carton picking situation.Note: MCL Voice does not support this configuration.

Determines when labels are printed during a voice picking assignment.• End of Assignment, No Verification: Labels are printed at the end of the assignment, and the operator is not asked to verify the label quantity or values.• End of Assignment, Verify Only Values: Labels are printed at the end of the assignment, but the operator does not need to specify the number of labels to print. Upon receiving the labels, the operator is required to speak each label number to the application for verification.• End of Assignment, Verify Quantity and Values: Labels are printed at the end of the assignment, and the operator must specify the number of labels to print. Upon receiving the labels, the operator is required to speak each label number to the application for verification.• Never Print: Labels are not printed during the assignment.• Start of Assignment: Labels are printed at the start of the picking assignment. MCL Voice does not support this configuration. Notes: • For pick work assignments, voice operators can speak "print labels" at any time after starting the work assignment to print labels for the LPNs on their device. If an operator speaks "print labels" at multiple points during a work assignment, labels are printed for all of the inventory on the device, even if the labels were previously printed. • If labels are automatically printed at the start of the assignment but the operator prints labels during the assignment, the labels will be reprinted. If labels are set to print at the end of an assignment but the operator prints them prior to ending the assignment, the application does not reprint the labels. If this field is set to Never Print, then printing labels is not allowed.

Location to which a partially picked carton is automatically deposited when picks in the current work zone are complete. This allows the carton to be picked up by a different operator to complete picks in the next work zone. This field is only available if the Work Zone Auto Deposit field is set to Yes.Select a location if you want the application to automatically deposit the partially picked carton. If left blank (no value), the operator selects a location after being notified that picks for the current work zone are complete.The location that you select must not belong to a movement zone that is designated as a hop in a movement path because hop locations are typically associated with release commands that generate work to move inventory to the next location in the path. For example, if the WRAP movement zone is a hop in the movement path, a location defined in the WRAP movement zone should not be used as a pick-and-pass location.Note: MCL Voice does not support this configuration.

If Yes, then for each picked LPN in a work assignment, the application generates a unique 4-digit value that the operator must speak to verify the LPN label. The random alphanumeric value generated by the application can include a combination of numbers 0 through 9 and letters A through F. The value can be printed on the LPN label, and the operator must verify each label using the application-generated value, instead of speaking the last 4 digits of the LPN.Notes: • Threshold picking does not support random label verification.• If you set this field to Yes, then for the application to print the value on the label, you must add the voc_chkdgt argument name (field) to the criteria for the pallet label document type. If you do not add the field, the number is still generated but not printed. See Add or modify a document type.If No, then the application does not generate a random label value, and voice operators must verify labels for picked LPNs by speaking the last 4 digits of an LPN.Only available if the Labels field is set to End of Assignment, Operator Verifies.

Maximum number of unsuccessful attempts that the voice device has to retrieve the next batch of picks from the application. When the number of attempts reaches this value, the application resolves the error and provides the next batch so the operator can continue the next assignment. Unsuccessful requests for a new batch can occur when the current assignment has unresolved picking errors.

Maximum number of picks sent to the voice device in a single batch. A lower value (minimum of 10) means the device needs to request new batches from the application more often; however, this configuration allows the operator to be informed of picking errors more frequently and address them immediately. A higher value means the device needs to stop picking less often to request a new batch from the application; however, if the application is using one-way messaging, the operator is not informed of picking errors until the current batch is complete.Note: You can define this field value in the general voice picking configurations and for a specific pick zone. The pick zone batch limit overrides the value defined in the voice picking configurations.When the number of picks on a device falls to 50% of the configured value, the application sends another batch limit of picks to the device. Therefore, the number of picks currently on a voice device can fluctuate between 50% and 150% of the defined batch limit. For example, if the defined limit is 10, then when there are 5 picks remaining on a device, the application sends 10 more picks so the device has a total of 15 picks.When the application creates a batch and adheres to the configured batch limit, it also considers the next pick in sequence (which would exceed the batch limit) to determine if it can be consolidated with the last pick in the previous batch based on item, location, and pick UOM. For example, assume the batch limit for voice picking is 10. If 11 separate picks exist for Item A from the same location and in the same picking UOM, then instead of sending separate batches to the voice device (one for the first 10 picks and another for the eleventh pick because it exceeds the limit), the application consolidates the quantity of the eleventh pick into the batch with the first 10 picks. The voice operator is then prompted with a single pick quantity to fulfill all 11 picks.Note: The application continues to evaluate and consolidate the next pick in sequence until it no longer matches the last pick in the original batch, or until 25 additional picks have been added to the original batch.

Number of subsequent picks in a work assignment that the application pre-validates. Pick pre-validation is a process that determines whether inventory is available in a location prior to presenting the pick to an operator.Note: You can define this field value in the general voice picking configurations and for a specific pick zone. The pick zone validation batch size overrides the value defined in the voice picking configurations.For example, assume the Pick Validation Batch Size is 5. When a voice operator acknowledges a work assignment and is directed to the first pick location, the application pre-validates the first 5 picks. After the operator completes 4 of the picks, there is one pre-validated pick remaining, and the operator is directed to the fifth pick. At the same time, the application pre-validates the next 5 picks in the work assignment.Set this field to a higher number in fast-moving or high-density picking environments to ensure the operator has a higher number of validated picks to complete over a short period of time. Alternatively, set this field to a lower number in slower moving picking environments or to reduce the need to skip or cancel picks that would fail validation. For example, if this field is set to 1 (default value) and the fourth pick requires a replenishment, then there is time for the replenishment to be completed before the application attempts to validate that pick. However, if the field was set to 4, then the fourth pick would fail validation without the replenishment completed, and the pick is subject to the fail action defined on the pick pre-validation scheme associated with the pick method. As another example, pick zones in which a voice device's connection to the application may be inhibited (such as a freezer) could be configured with a higher validation batch to reduce the number of transaction messages that are exchanged.Note: This field has no effect if the picked message format between the voice device and application is ODR (outbound data record). The application only pre-validates the Pick Validation Batch Size if the message format is LUT (look-up table). If the ODR format is used, the application pre-validates all of the picks issued to the device.

Determines the picked message format between the voice device and the application. A picked message is a communication that is sent from the device to the application when the operator completes a pick.• ODR - One way message: The device sends picked messages using outbound data record (ODR) format. ODR format enables the device to confirm that messages are received by the application while continuing with the next pick. The device does not wait for a pick to process before continuing and does not receive any message regarding the pick status. If the application cannot be reached by the device (for example, due to poor network connectivity), the ODR format causes the device to continuously attempt to process the information until it is received by the application; meanwhile, the operator can continue picking without stopping. If a picking error occurs using ODRs, the operator is notified when a new batch of picks is sent to the device.• LUT - Two way message, ODR on failure: The device sends picked messages using the look-up table (LUT) format. When using LUT, the device sends a picked message and waits for the application to process the pick before continuing with the next pick. If the device cannot reach the application, the message is converted to ODR format and the operator can continue picking while the device attempts to process the message. Any picking errors that occur while using LUT format are immediately reported to the operator.• LUT - Two way message format always: The device sends picked messages using the LUT format. This format is the same as the previous LUT format, but if the application cannot receive the message, continuous attempts are made in the LUT format. The operator must wait for the message to process before continuing with the next pick, and any picking errors are immediately reported to the operator.

If Yes, the voice device prompts the operator with a work estimate (in minutes) for the current picking work assignment. Labor future estimates must be configured for your application in order to receive spoken estimates. Goal time and assignment performance are only provided when Warehouse Management is integrated with Warehouse Labor Management.If No, the voice device does not provide a work estimate for the current work assignment.Note: MCL Voice does not support this configuration.

If Yes, the voice device speaks an estimate of the operator's previous assignment performance at the start of the next assignment. Only available when Warehouse Management is integrated with Warehouse Labor Management.If No, the voice device does not provide performance values.Note: MCL Voice does not support this configuration.
