The oldest inventory will be selected first.• LEFO-ORDER-BY and LEFO-ORDER-BY-ABSOLUTE: Last-expiration, first-out. The last inventory to expire will be selected first.• LIFO-ORDER-BY and LIFO-ORDER-BY-ABSOLUTE: Last-in, first-out. The newest inventory will be selected first. • LOCATION-ORDER-BY: Locations are ordered within a pick zone (maintaining the allocation search path order) by the location attributes specified for the Location Sort field in inventory selection settings.• No selection (blank): The application uses the inventory rotation method of the highest defined level of precedence. For information on precedence, see Inventory rotation allocation processing. Note: Inventory rotation methods defined at a lower precedence (except the default method) are automatically copied to the order line or work order line when the line is created. For example, if an order line is created for a date-tracked item with a rotation method defined, the rotation method is copied from the item to the order line, and then the application uses the order line rotation method during allocation.If no inventory rotation method is defined at any level, then the application uses the allocation search path sequence and allocates the first available inventory it finds that matches all of the required attributes. When using inventory rotation methods that are not absolute, the application searches for inventory by allocation search path in sequence until it finds a pick zone that contains the inventory, and then allocates inventory that is closest to the preferred processing date. Therefore, the application stops searching at the first pick zone in which matching inventory is found.When using absolute inventory rotation methods, the application searches either all of the allocation search paths for inventory that is closest to the preferred processing date or, if absolute groups are defined, each absolute group in sequence until it finds matching inventory and then allocates inventory that is closest to the preferred processing date from the pick zones within the absolute group. Therefore, the absolute method allows for more a comprehensive search to find the inventory.

Minimum number of hours away from expiration that a date-tracked item must be considered for allocation. For example, if this value is 10, then the application only allocates inventory that has at least 10 hours to reach its expiration date. Only available if the item specified on the order line is date-tracked.
Name that identifies a footprint, which describes the packaging dimensions and units of measure for the item with which it is associated.
Case configuration (number of units for each case) that allocated top-level items must have.
Inner pack configuration (number of units for each inner pack) that allocated top-level items must have.

Identifier for the levels of quality at which the customer is willing to accept inventory. The allocation profile is a prioritized list of inventory statuses that defines which statuses can be shipped. It is applied to both date-controlled and non-date-controlled inventory.

Indicates whether, when the inventory specified on the work order line is identified, it will be moved directly from its receiving point to a cross dock location or a specified staging location to satisfy an order or work order.

Indicates whether allocation is to automatically round up the pick quantity to the next highest unit of measure. The pick quantity may be rounded up only within the bounds defined by the values specified in the Over Allocation Amount and Over Allocation Code. This option is beneficial, for example, in situations where it is easier to pick an entire case or pallet instead of breaking a case or pallet to complete a pick.

Name of the allocation rule. An allocation rule is a processing command that specifies the inventory attribute values that are acceptable to fulfill an order line, work order detail, work order line, or bill of materials (BOM) detail.
Description that further defines the allocation rule.

Identifier that defines the type of customs tracking required for the inventory on the planned inbound order. The customs type can only be modified when the planned inbound order status is Excepted or Pending. Defining a customs type on the planned inbound order overrides the customs type defined for the items on the order. If you select a bonded customs type (Customs or Excise) for the entire order, you cannot override specific customs information for the items on the order lines. Only displayed if Customs functionality is enabled for the warehouse.• Blank (no selection): Customs related fields are available for edit on the order line. Customs information is based off the item if no customs information is defined on the order line.• Free: None of the inventory on this planned inbound order is under bond. Customs information is cleared from the order line and the customs related fields are not available for edit.• Customs: All of the inventory on this planned inbound order is under bond. Customs related fields on the order line are not available for edit, with the exception of the customs consignment ID.• Excise: All of the inventory on this planned inbound order is under bond and requires a duty stamp. Customs related fields on the order line are not available for edit, with the exception of the customs consignment ID.

Code for the value added tax (VAT) for the item. A customs VAT is charged on goods and some services that are imported from countries outside the European Unit (EU) and brought into the United Kingdom (UK) from other EU countries. It is also charged on most goods and services that VAT-registered businesses provide in the UK.• Standard: The standard customs VAT rate is charged for this item.• Zero: No customs VAT is charged for this item.

Code that identifies a commodity. Commodities are categories created to group inventory that has the same qualities and specifications, regardless of their source. For example, wheat is a commodity. Commodity codes are standardized to provide carriers with a standard by which to determine pricing and to simplify the shipment process. The Commodity Code is usually printed on the bill of lading (BOL). If the commodity is printed on the BOL, all products of the same commodity are totaled.

Country in which the item was manufactured. This value is displayed by default on the planned inbound order line for the item, but can be changed during receiving. Only available if the value for Customs Item Type is either Customs or Excise.
Indicates whether the item is duty stamp tracked or not. Only applies to items for which excise duties need to be paid.
Monetary amount that is paid to customs for the item. The amount is paid in the currency defined in the currency field. Only available if the Customs Item Type is either Customs or Excise.
Unique identifier for the work order type. A work order type is a category into which work orders are grouped based on similar processing characteristics.
Production line area in which the top-level item specified on this bill of material or work order will be assembled or disassembled.

Production line at which the top-level items for the BOM or work order are to be built. If you leave this field blank, the application will allocate a production line in the area selected from the Processing Area list. A production line is an arrangement of machines or sequence of operations (production stations) involved with a single manufacturing operation or production process.

Disassembly station at which the top-level items for the BOM or work order are to be broken down. A disassembly station is a position on a production line where a specific operation is performed during the disassembly of the top-level item (finished good). If you leave this field blank, the application will deliver the top-level items to the staging location of the specified production line, from which they can be moved to a station for disassembly.

Indicates that the work order type will be the default type for work orders that are automatically generated from this BOM. For example, if you set this field to Yes for an assembly work order type processing configuration, while you still can manually create assembly and disassembly work orders using this BOM, when a work order is automatically generated using this BOM, the work order type is Assembly. There can only be one default generation work order type for a BOM.
Unique identifier for the bill of material line.

Unique identifier for an item and the name of the client who stores the inventory in the facility. This is the client that houses the item specified in the work order and is not necessarily the client that created the work order. Only displayed in a 3PL environment.

Quantity (in terms of material handling or stock keeping units) of the component item required to assemble one top-level item. This is the quantity of the component item that will be consumed when assembling the top-level item. If a BOM is defined for the top-level item, then this value can be populated by the BOM.

Total amount of inventory that can be allocated over the requested quantity when the allocation code is Quantity, or percentage of inventory that can be allocated when the allocation code is Percentage.

Indicates whether allocation is to automatically round up the pick quantity to the next highest unit of measure. The pick quantity may be rounded up only within the bounds defined by the values specified in the Over Allocation Amount and Over Allocation Code. This option is beneficial, for example, in situations where it is easier to pick an entire case or pallet instead of breaking a case or pallet to complete a pick.

Identifier assigned to a quantity of inventory that is uniquely identified during the manufacturing process for the purpose of tracking an attribute of that inventory, such as its expiration date. Lots differentiate distinct groups of inventory that have the same item. Lots are user defined and are not necessarily unique since the same lot can be applied to different items. However, lot and item number combinations must be unique.

Default number of items per packaging type. For example, for the Each/Case packaging type, it is the quantity of pieces or eaches of the item that is typically received in a single case. If a pallet of the item is received with a different quantity in the cases, the receiver can change the Each/Case value for that specific pallet. This field is not available if you select a footprint code for the item.

Identifier for the levels of quality at which the customer is willing to accept inventory. The allocation profile is a prioritized list of inventory statuses that defines which statuses can be shipped. It is applied to both date-controlled and non-date-controlled inventory.
Indicates that the application will allocate the component inventory based on catch unit quantity instead of material handling (stock keeping) quantity.

Name of the allocation rule. An allocation rule is a processing command that specifies the inventory attribute values that are acceptable to fulfill an order line, work order detail, work order line, bill of materials (BOM), or BOM detail.
Catch unit amount of the component item required to assemble one top-level item. This is the catch unit quantity of the component item that will be consumed when assembling the top-level item.

Value that determines the minimum and maximum percentage of the BOM quantity (specified in the BOM Quantity field) for the component item that the application will allow. For example, if you enter a Consumption Tolerance Percentage of 10, then you can consume anywhere from 90% to 110% of the specified consumed quantity when assembling the top-level item.
Date and time at which the BOM was created.

Indicates whether, when the inventory specified on the work order line is identified, it will be moved directly from its receiving point to a cross dock location or a specified staging location to satisfy an order or work order.
Date and time indicating when the BOM was last modified.

Amount of time in relation to the inventory’s received date or expiration date during which inventory is considered the same age for allocation when one of the FEFO/FIFO/LEFO/LIFO or absolute FEFO/FIFO/LEFO/LIFO inventory rotation methods is required.
Unit of time (minutes, hours, or days) for the outbound date window.

Value that determines the minimum and maximum percentage of the BOM quantity (specified in the BOM Quantity field) for the component item that the application will allow being scrapped (not reusable). For example, if you enter a scrap percentage of 50, then you can scrap anywhere from 50% to 150% of the specified BOM quantity when disassembling the top-level item.
Name that identifies a footprint, which describes the packaging dimensions and units of measure for the item with which it is associated.
User who created the BOM.

Value that represents the order in which the allocation process selects available inventory for allocation. Select an inventory rotation method if you want the application to search for inventory based on date processing or location.• FEFO-ORDER-BY and FEFO-ORDER-BY-ABSOLUTE: First-expiration, first-out. The first inventory to expire will be selected first.• FIFO-ORDER-BY and FIFO-ORDER-BY-ABSOLUTE: First-in, first-out. The oldest inventory will be selected first.• LEFO-ORDER-BY and LEFO-ORDER-BY-ABSOLUTE: Last-expiration, first-out. The last inventory to expire will be selected first.• LIFO-ORDER-BY and LIFO-ORDER-BY-ABSOLUTE: Last-in, first-out. The newest inventory will be selected first. When using inventory rotation methods that are not absolute, the application searches for inventory by allocation search path in sequence until it finds a pick zone that contains the inventory, and then allocates inventory that is closest to the preferred processing date. Therefore, the application stops searching at the first pick zone in which matching inventory is found.When using absolute inventory rotation methods, the application searches either all of the allocation search paths for inventory that is closest to the preferred processing date or, if absolute groups are defined, it searches each absolute group in sequence until it finds matching inventory and then allocates inventory that is closest to the preferred processing date from the pick zones within the absolute group. Therefore, the absolute method allows for more a comprehensive search to find the inventory.

Defines the quality or disposition of the inventory. This is the default inventory status that is displayed when an operator identifies completed top-level items for the work order. However, the operator may change the status. Only available for assembly work orders.
Name of the person who last modified the BOM.

Minimum number of hours away from expiration that a date-tracked item must be considered for allocation. For example, if this value is 10, then the application only allocates inventory that has at least 10 hours to reach its expiration date. Only available if the item specified on the order line is date-tracked.
Unique identifier for this instance of the work order, which enables you to use a standard work order multiple times.

Indicates that this component item will not be allocated when work orders based on this bill of material or work order are allocated. This option is useful for packaging or supply items that must be tracked for cost purposes, but not picked, because they are often stored in a work-in-process supply location type.

Identifier that is an attribute of an item or item and lot combination and is assigned by the item's supplier. A supplier lot number used to uniquely identify and track the inventory to which it is assigned. The supplier lot number is a different attribute than the lot number, which is a manufacturer or production lot number.
Unique identifier for the work order type. A work order type is a category into which work orders are grouped based on similar processing characteristics.

Area in your facility in which the production line is located. This production area is used as a default area for work orders of this type. If a production area is not assigned to a work order, the application uses the default production area specified for the work order type.

If Yes, work orders of this type are used for the disassembly of top-level items. Select Yes if work orders of this type are processed by picking top-level items, which are then delivered to a production line and disassembled into component items to be identified.If No, work orders of this type are used for assembling picked component items into top-level items to be identified.
Description that further defines the work order type.

Identifier for a production line in the selected production area. The production line is used as a default for work orders of this type. If a production line is not assigned to a work order, the application uses the default production line specified for the work order type.

If Yes, work orders created using this work order type are eligible for bulk pick processing. Bulk pick processing allocates matching inventory for multiple work order lines together into larger unit of measure (UOM) picks so as to reduce the number of smaller UOM picks required to satisfy the orders. Select Yes if work orders created using this work order type should be considered by the application when allocating inventory using bulk picking.If No, work orders created using this work order type are not considered for bulk picking. Instead, the required inventory for the work order is allocated and picked separately.The Bulk Picking field is only displayed if bulk picking is enabled for the warehouse.
Workstation device that is used to access Production Line Operations.
Area in which the production lines are located. The workstation can be used to access Production Line Operations to view and manage production lines in the selected area.

If Yes, then in Production Line Operations, the user can view processing areas other than the one to which the workstation is assigned.If No, the user is able to view and manage only the production lines assigned to the selected area.
Identifier used to group similar items together. Typically, all of the items within a family have the same material handling characteristics.
Storage area to which finished goods that belong to an item family are automatically moved when those finished goods are identified
Location in the selected area to which finished goods that belong to an item family are automatically moved when those finished goods are identified.
Default inbound order type that is created when inventory is identified from a production line.

Type of allocation that is performed for a work order.• Order Picks: Commit inventory, create pick work entries, and create shipment information. Replenishments are not created, even if inventory is missing.• Order Picks and Replenishments: Commit inventory, create pick work entries, and create any needed replenishments. This option is typically selected since top-level items cannot be created without all of the component items.• Replenishments: Creates any needed replenishments.• Top-off Replenishment: Creates any needed top-off replenishments.
Valid server command that is executed when picks are released from a hold status. This command runs after the PROCESS PICK RELEASE command.
Valid server command that is executed when inventory that had been allocated for a work order is deallocated. This command is run after the DEALLOCATE WORK ORDER command.

Validation or processing server command, based on work order revision, client, and warehouse that is executed prior to allocation. Typically used to validate a work order configuration, this command is run before the CREATE WORK ORDER command. If validation is not successful, then allocation does not occur.
Valid server command that is executed when picks that were allocated to a hold status are confirmed without being released. This command runs after the CONFIRM PICKS FOR WORK ORDERS command.
Valid server command that is executed when a work order is allocated. The command is run after the ALLOCATE WORK ORDER command.

If Yes, then during disassembly, if an operator identifies a component item that does not belong to the disassembly work order, a message is displayed to the operator. The message allows the operator to select whether to continue identifying the component item and adding it to the disassembly work order.If No, then if an operator identifies a component item that is not included on the disassembly work order, an error message is displayed and the operator is not allowed to identify the item as a component of the work order.

field: Allow Close When Expected Scrap Percentage Exceeded
description: If Yes, the application allows an operator to close a disassembly work order when the components exceed the expected scrap percentage defined for the work order. If set to Yes, then when an operator attempts to close a disassembly work order for which the component scraps exceed the expected percentage, a warning message is displayed and the operator can choose whether to close the work order or not.If No, the application does not allow an operator to close a disassembly work order when the component scraps exceed the expected percentage defined for the work order.

If Yes, the application automatically creates a work order setup when the component items of a work order are delivered to a production line or station. If set to Yes, the application uses the attribute values specified for the component items that are attribute-tracked and creates the work order setup. After the top-level item is identified, the attribute values are displayed when identifying the component items used to build the top-level item.If No, then work order setups are not created automatically.

Default supplier used for inventory that is identified from a production line. A supplier can be an individual, organization, or another warehouse within your own organization from which you repeatedly receive inventory or handling units.

Identifier for a prioritized list of inventory statuses that defines which statuses can be shipped. This is the default allocation profile that is assigned to a work order line that is generated automatically. A work order line is generated automatically when an operator delivers inventory to a production line, and the inventory does not match the inventory defined on any existing work order line.

field: Allow Restricted Lot Status for Work Orders
description: If Yes, component inventory from restricted item lots can be allocated for work orders. The restricted status can indicate, for example, a safety issue within a specific lot or that the inventory requires testing or validation before it can be shipped to an end customer. When restricted component inventory is built into finished goods, if component tracking is not enabled, the application does not track the restricted inventory. For this reason, some facilities prevent restricted inventory from being used to fulfill a work order.If No, component inventory from restricted item lots cannot be allocated for work orders.

If Yes, the application checks consumption tolerances by LPN. The consumption tolerance, defined for a work order line, represents the minimum and maximum percentage of a consumed quantity that is allowed for the component item in building finished goods. Select Yes if you want to evaluate consumption tolerance for each LPN that is identified.If No, the application checks consumption tolerances by work order, after all of the LPNs for the work order have been identified.

field: Close Work Order Automatically When Complete
description: If Yes, the application automatically closes the work order after all of the component inventory is either consumed, returned to stock, or returned to the work in process supply area. If set to Yes, the application also closes a work order automatically when finished goods are identified and the work order quantity is fulfilled.If No, the application does not automatically close the work order.

If Yes, the Item field is displayed on the RF Production screen, which allows the operator to scan an item or alternate item to find the production line and work order from which to start receiving. If set to Yes, then if an operator scans an alternate item, such as a universal product code (UPC), the application attempts to match an in-progress work order with the item. If multiple items associated with the alternate item are expected for in-progress work orders, the operator is prompted to select the correct item to receive.If No, the Item field is not displayed on the RF Productions screen. Instead, the operator starts receiving by entering a production line or work order.

If Yes, an operator can start to identify finished goods before all of the component items or pending picks required to complete the work order have not been delivered to the production area. Select Yes if you allow LPNs to be identified prior to all of the required inventory arriving at the production line.If No, the application does not allow operators to start identifying inventory from a production line until all of the required component items or pending picks are delivered to the production line.

If Yes, then during the work order completion process, the user can add unexpected component inventory after finished goods have been identified. Select Yes if you want to allow the user to add a work order detail for component inventory that was not allocated for the work order but was consumed in building the work order's top-level item.If No, the user is not allowed to add a work order detail for component inventory that was not allocated for the work order but was consumed in building the work order's top-level item.

field: Allow Cross Dock of Produced Inventory
description: If Yes, then when you create a new assembly or disassembly work order, the Allow Cross Dock of Produced Inventory field on the work order (assembly) or work order line (disassembly) is set to Yes by default. Therefore, the inventory produced from the work order or work order line can be cross docked. If the inventory can fulfill a cross dock, when it is identified, it is moved directly from production receiving to a cross dock location or a staging location to satisfy an outbound order.If No, then when you create a new assembly or disassembly work order, the Allow Cross Dock of Produced Inventory field on the work order (assembly) or work order line (disassembly) is set to No by default. Therefore, the inventory produced from the work order or order line cannot be cross docked.Note: You can override this configuration for an assembly work order or a disassembly work order line.

Amount of time that must elapse before information on the Production Line Operations window is refreshed. Production Line Operations displays the processing status of work orders that have been assigned to production lines. The information includes progress information for picks, replenishments, and cross docks.

Integer value representing the maximum number of identical LPNs (full pallets) that a user is allowed to identify at one time from a production line. Allowing a user to identify multiple pallets of the same item at one time reduces the amount of data entry required. The user is prompted to provide a different LPN for each pallet, but only has to enter the attribute values once for the set of identical LPNs received.

Minimum number of characters that the application accepts when an LPN is scanned or typed into an LPN field during the identification of inventory from a production line. If the entered value falls outside of the range (for example, if a larger bar code number is scanned into the LPN field), then the application does not accept that value.

Maximum number of characters that the application accepts when an LPN is scanned or typed into an LPN field during the identification of inventory from a production line. If the entered value falls outside of the range (for example, if a shorter bar code number is scanned into the LPN field), then the application does not accept that value.

Unique identifier for the label format. This identifier must match the name (label ID) of the label as specified in Label Designer. For example, if you create a label for pallet building with the label identifier pallbl, then the value in this field should be pallbl. Label Designer is the default label service for Warehouse Management. See Label Designer overview.If Label Designer is disabled (LABEL-EDITOR policy removed), then this identifier must match the name of the file that contains the label configuration information, without the file extension. For example, if the file name is palletlabel.pof, then the value in this field should be palletlabel. For more information on custom label configuration files, contact your Blue Yonder project team.Note: The value for the Description field, rather than the label format identifier, is used during warehouse processing when the label format is displayed to users.
Meaningful description of the label format. This description, rather than the label format identifier, is used during warehouse processing when the label format is displayed to users.

MOCA data command that generates the label. For example, if you want the pallet build label to be generated during the pallet build process, then the value in Data Command field should be pallbl datacmd.Note: This field is only valid if Label Designer is enabled.
Default printer used to print the report or label. If, at the time of printing, the user does not specify a printer, then printing takes place at the default printer.

Variable name of the field to include on the label. This is the name that the application uses to display a label for the field. For example, stoloc displays the label for the Location field; ship_id displays the label for the Shipment field. To find an argument name, navigate to the Message Catalog page, and search for the field label using the MLS Text field.

If Yes, a value is required for the field. If set to Yes, then if the application cannot retrieve a value for the field, the document will not be produced.If No, a value is not required for the field.

Unique identifier for the document type. The document type is an internal application identifier. The application provides several common document types. If you need to add a new report or label format, instead of adding a new document type, you may only need to modify an existing document type and add the new format.
Category that determines whether the document type is a label or report.

Server command that retrieves the information to be printed on the report or label for the document type. The application performs this action when the document type is printed. Contact your Blue Yonder project team if you do not know what command to enter. Do not change the command without first consulting your project team.
Description of the document type. The description is the text that identifies the document type to users.

Value that specifies the shipping level at which the document type is printed.• Load: The document type is printed for the outbound load.• Stop: The document type is printed for each stop on the outbound load.• Shipment: The document type is printed for each shipment on the outbound load.
Reserved for future use.

Packaging level or unit of measure (UOM) for which the document type is printed if an LPN level or UOM is not specified at the time of printing.• LPN Level: Displays the Default LPN Levels field for you to select the packaging levels at which the label is printed. Packaging levels are defined on the item footprint configuration.• Unit of Measure: Displays the Default Units of Measure field for you to select the UOMs for which the label is printed, and whether it is printed for partial UOMs. UOMs are defined on the item footprint configuration.

LPN level for which the label is printed. At the time of printing, if the user does not select an LPN level and if an LPN level was not defined for the label compliance, then the default LPN level is used.• LPN: Inventory at the full LPN level; typically, a pallet. • Sub-LPN: Inventory at the case level.• Detail LPN: Inventory at the each (or piece) level.The Default LPN Levels field is only available if the Print Documents By field is set to LPN Level. In addition, you cannot change the LPN level if a compliance configuration already exists for the document type.

Label format or report format to which the compliance applies. The document format is a specific report or label format that you want to configure for printing, for example, based on customer preferences or for specific items. For example, if the document type is a bill of lading report, then you can define compliance for the standard bill of lading report and for each custom bill of lading report (such as those designed for specific customers or carriers).

Method to determine which printer to use to print the document.• Device code for workstation/Device: Use printer based on workstation or RF device associated with the action that initiated the report or label printing.• Destination Location: Use printer based on the destination location of the work.• Report's default printer: Use printer based on the report's or label's default printer.• Source Location: Use printer based on the source location of the work.• No selection (blank): Use printer based on the report's or label's default printer.IMPORTANT: If you select either the Report's default printer or No selection (blank) options and the report or label format does not have a default printer configured, then the report or label will not be printed.

Field that is used to determine which locale to apply to the report or label. A locale defines the culture-specific attributes displayed or printed on the report or label. Culture-specific attributes include language, time and date formats, currency formats, and measurement unit system.For example, if you ship to a foreign country, you can select to print the shipping documentation based on the locale of the ship-to customer.If you set the Locale Type field to Specific Locale, then the Locale field is displayed for you to select a locale. If you set the Locale Type field to Specific User, then the report is printed in the locale associated with the user who printed the label or report.

Identifier that determines the culture-specific attributes displayed or printed on the report or label. Culture-specific attributes include language, time and date formats, currency formats, and measurement unit system.

LPN level for which the label is printed. The LPN level only applies to label formats. If you leave this field blank, the document prints at the default LPN levels defined for the document type.• LPN: Inventory at the full LPN level; typically, a pallet. • Sub-LPN: Inventory at the case level.• Detail LPN: Inventory at the each (or piece) level.

Point in the warehouse process at which the application automatically prints the labels or reports. If you want a document format to be printed at multiple exit points, you must create a separate compliance configuration for each exit point.
Number of copies of the label or report to print at the selected exit point.

Optional user-defined text used to group document formats for the purpose of overriding the precedence of the compliance configurations. See Document groups and Precedence in compliance.The application does not validate the value that you enter in this field. Be sure to enter the text exactly as it is displayed in other document formats that you want to include in the same group. The value is case-sensitive; for example, the application does not regard BOL, Bol, and bol as the same document group.

Operator that is used with a value to qualify the criteria. For example, use "=" to limit the criteria to a specific value, such as Item Family = Apparel.• !=: Not equal to• =: Equal to• >: Greater than• >=: Greater than or equal to• <: Less than• <=: Less than or equal to

Value for the criteria. The value is used to limit use of the document format to matching inventory. For example, if the criteria is Item Family, you can use the operator and value to indicate the specific item family for which the document is used.

If Enabled, then the configuration settings will take effect. Also, if Event Management is installed, Event Management functionality becomes available for use in Warehouse Management.If Disabled, then Event Management processing functions will not take place. Also, if Event Management is installed, then Event Management functionality is disabled. For information on managing user and role access to disabled functionality, see Event Management integration.

Identifier for the current application (Warehouse Management) that is the source of alerts that are sent to Event Management. The value in this field is not used in any functional processing; instead, this value is used as the value for the Source System field on an alert notification in Event Management. The source of an Event Management alert can help users identify and focus on the alerts from a specific application. For example, if alerts are being sent to Event Management from Warehouse Management and from other systems, you could define this value as WM. Whenever information is sent to Event Management from Warehouse Management, the alert subscriber can immediately identify that the source system is WM and not one of the other systems. This field has a maximum of 30 characters.

If Yes, information is sent to Event Management whenever a download is placed in error status. A download is an inbound communication through Integrator.If No, information is not sent to Event Management.

If Yes, information is sent to Event Management whenever a download is created without any of the IFDs that are identified in Integrator. A download is an inbound communication through Integrator.If No, information is not sent to Event Management.

If Yes, information is sent to Event Management when the system encounters one or more errors when fully validating an inbound integration transaction.Note: You can configure the application to fully validate certain inbound integration transactions. See General Integration.If No, information is not sent to Event Management.

If Yes, information is sent to Event Management whenever a communication set (one or more interface documents [IFDs]) was not sent to the destination system and the events are placed in the send error (SE) status.If No, information is not sent to Event Management.

If Yes, information is sent to Event Management whenever Integrator cannot log a vendor inbound quality event.If No, information is not sent to Event Management.

If Yes, information is sent to Event Management whenever a shipment fails address validation or carrier selection by an integrated parcel system. See Parcel address validation and carrier selection.If No, information is not sent to Event Management.

If Yes, information is sent to Event Management whenever an error occurs while purging shipments. This notifies you about a problem that needs to be researched and corrected.If No, information is not sent to Event Management.

If Yes, information is sent to Event Management whenever transport equipment arrives before its scheduled appointment time. You specify the number of minutes before the scheduled appointment time that inbound transport equipment is considered early and Event Management is notified.If No, information is not sent to Event Management.

If Yes, information is sent to Event Management whenever transport equipment arrives after its scheduled appointment time. You specify the number of minutes after the scheduled appointment time that inbound transport equipment is considered late and Event Management is notified.If No, information is not sent to Event Management.

field: Handling Unit Feature Out of Threshold
description: If Yes, information is sent to Event Management whenever the value of a handling unit feature falls outside threshold values set for the feature. For example, if your handling unit feature is transport equipment temperature, you can set threshold values for that feature; if the transport equipment temperature is higher or lower than the threshold values, and this policy is enabled, then a notice is sent to Event Management. This event only applies to handling unit types configured with the Transport Equipment handling unit category.If No, information is not sent to Event Management.

field: Handling Units at Location Below the Stocking Level
description: If Yes, information is sent to Event Management whenever the quantity of a specified handling unit type falls below the minimum value defined for the location. For example, if a location is configured to have a minimum of 15 handling units of a certain handling unit type and the quantity of handling units in the location falls to 14, then a notification is sent to Event Management if this policy is enabled. This event only applies to handling unit types configured with the Inventory handling unit category.If No, information is not sent to Event Management.

If Yes, information is sent to Event Management whenever a handling unit is not moved within the specified number of hours. For example, if you define a slow moving handling unit as one that has not moved in 10 hours and a handling unit is stationary for longer than 10 hours, then a notification is sent to Event Management if this policy is enabled. This event only applies to handling unit types configured with the Inventory handling unit category.If No, information is not sent to Event Management.
If Yes, information is sent to Event Management whenever an error is returned during the processing of a server command for a background workflow.If No, information is not sent to Event Management.

If Yes, information is sent to Event Management whenever an error is returned during the processing of a server command for an inbound or outbound workflow.If No, information is not sent to Event Management.

If Yes, information is sent to Event Management whenever an error is returned during the processing of a server command for warehouse equipment, transport equipment, or a production workflow.If No, information is not sent to Event Management.

If Yes, information is sent to Event Management whenever pickable inventory becomes stranded. Inventory can become stranded (not pickable) if an operator overrides a warning message and deposits inventory in a location in a zone that does not support picking the unit of measure (UOM) that was deposited. For example, if a zone supports only picking pallets and an operator overrides a warning message and deposits cases of inventory to the location, those cases would be stranded because cases are not pickable in that location.If No, information is not sent to Event Management.

If Yes, information is sent to Event Management whenever there is a discrepancy when an operator performs a count back. Count back is a picking verification to capture the quantity that is remaining in a pallet or location in addition to the quantity being picked from the pallet.If count back is required for an operator picking less than a full pallet, a count back discrepancy exists when the remaining quantity does not match the expected quantity. If this policy is enabled, then whenever there is a count back discrepancy, a notification is sent to Event Management.If No, information is not sent to Event Management.

If Yes, information is sent to Event Management whenever a location within your warehouse is placed in an error condition (occurs when the Location Status is Inventory Error). This means that a discrepancy was found between the items in the location and the item information for that location; for example, a different physical quantity than the quantity indicated in the application. When a location is in error, inventory cannot be allocated from or putaway (deposited) in it. Consequently, you might want to know about locations in error quickly so that the problem can be resolved and the location reset to a usable status.If No, information is not sent to Event Management.

If Yes, information is sent to Event Management whenever a lot for which inventory exists in the warehouse is nearing its expiration date. You specify the number of days in advance of the expiration date and Event Management is notified.If No, information is not sent to Event Management.

If Yes, information is sent to Event Management whenever the inventory level for an item in the facility falls below the reorder point defined for the item. If Low Inventory is enabled, then the application periodically checks each item to see if the amount of inventory in your facility is less than the amount set as the re-order point defined for the item. If it is, then the application notifies Event Management of low inventory.If No, information is not sent to Event Management.

field: Work Order with Unassigned Detail Started
description: If Yes, information is sent to Event Management whenever a user starts a work order that has one or more details that have not yet been assigned to a production station.If No, information is not sent to Event Management.

If Yes, information is sent to Event Management whenever the application automatically generates a work order from a bill of material (BOM) that has the Auto-generate Work Order check box selected. Work orders are automatically created from a BOM when an order, work order, or replenishment for the top-level item is allocated, and the application cannot find the inventory in the facility.Work orders are also automatically created when an order line that specifies order explosion (the Item Download Type field, PRT_DL_TYP, is set to K for kit) is downloaded from the host system. Order explosion is an order processing mode in which an order for a top-level item is downloaded from the host system, and the application converts the order into an order for the component items, as defined by a BOM for the top-level item.If No, information is not sent to Event Management.

If Yes, information is sent to Event Management whenever a carton is resized for picking. The Carton Resize function enables you to assign a different carton code to an existing carton number being used for picking. If you are picking into a carton and realize it is too large or too small for the order, you can reassign a carton code to the existing carton number, which provides you with the proper dimensions to complete the picks.If No, information is not sent to Event Management.

field: Item Lot Created or Changed by Download
description: If Yes, information is sent to Event Management when the application successfully creates or updates an item lot record due to a status change request sent from the host. Warehouses may receive a request to update the default receiving status of inbound inventory that matches the attributes defined in the request, including the item and lot combination.For example, in a third-party logistics environment, assume that a warehouse receives Client A's inventory for a specific item lot combination in the Available status. If Client A discovers an issue with the item lot, the client can send a request to update the status assigned to that item lot combination so that when additional inventory is received, the application applies the new inventory status. In addition, the application attempts to update existing inventory in the warehouse with the same item lot combination to the new inventory status.If this field is set to Yes, information is sent to Event Management only when the application receives the transaction and successfully updates (if the record exists) or creates a new item lot record with the attributes provided in the transaction. This event is not dependent on whether the application successfully processes the actual status change for existing inventory in the warehouse that matches the item lot record.The event contains the inventory status change request details, of which the following are required:• Warehouse• Client• Item• Lot• From Status• To StatusIf No, information is not sent to Event Management.

If Yes, information is sent to Event Management when the application successfully processes an inventory status change due to a request received from the host to update the default status of inventory received with a certain item and lot combination.Warehouses may receive a request to update the default receiving status of inbound inventory that matches the attributes defined in the request, including the item and lot combination.For example, in a third-party logistics environment, assume that a warehouse receives Client A's inventory for a specific item lot combination in the Available status. If Client A discovers an issue with the item lot, the client can send a request to update the status assigned to that item lot combination so that when additional inventory is received, the application applies the new inventory status. In addition, the application attempts to update existing inventory in the warehouse with the same item lot combination to the new inventory status. If enabled, this event is used to notify Event Management when the application successfully updates the status of existing inventory in the warehouse to the new inventory status.The event contains the inventory status change request details, of which the following are required:• Warehouse• Client• Item• Lot• From Status• To StatusIf No, information is not sent to Event Management.

field: Inventory Status Error During Change by Download
description: If Yes, information is sent to Event Management when the application cannot successfully process an inventory status change due to a request received from the host.Warehouses may receive a request to update the default receiving status of inbound inventory that matches the attributes defined in the request, including the item and lot combination.For example, in a third-party logistics environment, assume that a warehouse receives Client A's inventory for a specific item lot combination in the Available status. If Client A discovers an issue with the item lot, the client can send a request to update the status assigned to that item lot combination so that when additional inventory is received, the application applies the new inventory status. In addition, the application attempts to update existing inventory in the warehouse with the same item/lot combination to the new inventory status. If enabled, this event is used to notify Event Management when the application cannot successfully update the status of existing inventory in the warehouse to the new inventory status due to a processing error.This alert can be sent, for example, if the application cannot process the status change because it would violate a mixing rule. The event contains the inventory status change request details, of which the following are required:• Warehouse• Client• Item• Lot• From Status• To StatusIf No, information is not sent to Event Management.

If Yes, information is sent to Event Management whenever a new item is created with the Receivable field set to No. The Receivable field is set to No for an item to indicate that not all of the valid information that is needed to store and ship the item is available. Generally, this is the case when new item information is sent to Warehouse Management from a host system when the host system does not have all the necessary item information. Whenever an item is created that is not receivable, a notification is sent to Event Management.If No, information is not sent to Event Management.

If Yes, information is sent to Event Management whenever an outbound audit is completed with discrepancies. A discrepancy occurs when the attribute value entered by the operator is different from what the application expected.If No, information is not sent to Event Management.

Cancel code configurations allow you to indicate whether a notification should be sent when a pick is canceled using the code.If No, information is not sent to Event Management.

field: Duty for Customs Consignment is Not Processed
description: If Yes, information is sent to Event Management whenever picking has occurred for bonded inventory and the customs consignment has not been processed by a duty management application. A customs consignment is set of customs-related information that is associated with a specific receipt of bonded inventory. This event is sent to prioritize the sending of customs consignment to the duty management application. If enabled, then whenever picking has occurred for bonded inventory and the customs consignment has not been processed, a notification is sent to Event ManagementIf No, information is not sent to Event Management.

If this field is set to Yes, then each time an error occurs while an operator completes a voice pick, a notification is sent to Event Management.If No, information is not sent to Event Management.

If Yes, information is sent to Event Management whenever a work order replenishment is cancelled due to application timeout or error conditions, and that corrective action is needed to regenerate the work order replenishment task.If No, information is not sent to Event Management.

If Yes, information is sent to Event Management whenever a sequenced order pick is cancelled and either not reallocated, partially reallocated, or unsuccessfully reallocated. Picks for sequenced orders are planned to work assignments by item family set. Each order is planned to a specific slot on a master handling unit; and the slot is reserved for the order. If nothing is found in reallocation, the slot is reserved (not used) and the remaining picks for the handling unit are directed to the slots for which they were planned.If No, information is not sent to Event Management.

If Yes, information is sent to Event Management whenever an operator enters a deposit quantity of 0 at the replenishment destination location in a movement zone enabled for splitting replenishment residuals. See Splitting replenishment residuals.

If Yes, information is sent to Event Management whenever transport equipment is marked hot, meaning that it contains inventory needed to complete an order and should receive priority in unloading.If No, information is not sent to Event Management.

field: Auto Create Putaway Fails on Transport Equipment Close
description: If Yes, information is sent to Event Management when the application fails to create directed work to store staged inventory when configured to do so. The information lists the LPNs for which directed work was not created. The application may fail to create directed work, for example, if a suitable storage location could not be found for the inventory.This event is only used if the application is configured to create directed work automatically for staged inventory after an RF operator closes transport equipment. See Automatic creation of directed putaway.If No, information is not sent to Event Management.

If Yes, information is sent to Event Management whenever the estimated number of pallets required for the shipments assigned to a particular carrier that have not yet been assigned to stops has exceeded your threshold limit. This information indicates that someone should contact the carrier to let them know that they need to send transport equipment to pick up the shipments.For example, you can set the threshold to the number of pallets that fills a single piece of transport equipment. Whenever the threshold is exceeded, you know that you will soon have enough shipments ready to fill the transport equipment and should contact the carrier to send another. Then, while the carrier is en route and the operators finish staging the shipments, you can set up everything that you need to set up in the application before loading the transport equipment, such as a load and stops. You specify the number of pallets that needs to be exceeded before Event Management is notified.If No, information is not sent to Event Management.

If Yes, information is sent to Event Management whenever an error occurs when applying deferred changes to a shipment. Changes are deferred when a shipment is in-process and then applied after the shipment has been staged so you know that there is a problem that needs to be researched and corrected.If No, information is not sent to Event Management.

If Yes, information is sent to Event Management whenever a change to a Transportation Manager-planned shipment has been deferred because the shipment has been allocated but not yet staged. The change will take effect when the shipment has been staged. This event's primary use is to let the Event Management alert subscriber know that a carrier change was made to the shipment, but the carrier change is not visible in the application until the shipment is staged. This information lets the Event Management alert subscriber know that once the shipment is staged, it may need to be moved to a different ship staging location (the location that services the new carrier).If No, information is not sent to Event Management.

If Yes, information is sent to Event Management whenever a shipment is about to be late; that is, the staged shipment has not yet been loaded onto transport equipment and it is within a specified number of hours of reaching the Late Ship Date. For example, if you set the threshold for this policy to 4, the Late Ship Date for the order is today at 5 P.M., it is 2 P.M. and the shipment has not been shipped, then Event Management is notified.If No, information is not sent to Event Management.

This notifies a subscriber to this Event Management event that the shipment needs to be manually staged. If you want the application to notify Event Management whenever a pick is cancelled in general, configure the pick cancellation settings.If No, information is not sent to Event Management.

If Yes, information is sent to Event Management whenever an error occurs during the parcel manifest process. This notifies you about a problem that needs to be researched and corrected.If No, information is not sent to Event Management.

field: Distribution Order Scheduled To Ship Before Distribution Inventory Scheduled To Be Received
description: If Yes, information is sent to Event Management when a distribution is created with a ship date that is earlier than the date on which the inventory is expected to be received.If No, information is not sent to Event Management.
If Yes, information is sent to Event Management whenever a shipment has been shipped without the entire requested quantity (shipped short).If No, information is not sent to Event Management.

If Yes, information is sent to Event Management whenever a shipment has been staged in your warehouse for more than a certain number of hours. You specify the number of hours that need to pass before a shipment is considered stalled and Event Management is notified. More specifically, you may want to know when a shipment is waiting in staging because its last pick was cancelled.If No, information is not sent to Event Management.

If Yes, information is sent to Event Management whenever the application detects an in-transit shipment that has not been processed in a specified period of time. This informs a shipping site that the receiving site never received the advance shipment notification (ASN) information from the host system. This notifies you about a problem that needs to be researched and corrected.If No, information is not sent to Event Management.

If Yes, information is sent to Event Management whenever transport equipment is closed. This event information is useful in that users managing transport equipment closures can be immediately notified whenever a transport equipment is closed.If No, information is not sent to Event Management.

If Yes, information is sent to Event Management whenever the application sends an Integrator transaction (SHIPMENT_STATUS_CHANGE) to notify the host that a client's shipment has reached a certain status. For example, if for CLIENT A you select the Loaded status for notifications, then whenever a shipment for that client transitions to Loaded, the application sends a transaction to the host, which raises this event. See Configure outbound paperwork.If No, information is not sent to Event Management.

If Yes, information is sent to Event Management whenever a shipping container cannot be closed due to an out of tolerance weight issue. When the packing operator attempts to close a shipping container, an error occurs when the difference between the estimated and actual weight of the container exceeds the acceptable minimum or maximum tolerance limit. If the error occurs, the information is sent to Event Management.If No, information is not sent to Event Management.

If Yes, information is sent to Event Management whenever an order line is updated to indicate that a discrepancy exists between the quantity that was shipped and the quantity that the customer reported as received.If No, information is not sent to Event Management.

If Yes, information is sent to Event Management whenever an error occurs during processing of a Warehouse Management order into a Transportation Manager order. This notifies you about a problem that needs to be researched and corrected.If No, information is not sent to Event Management.

If Yes, information is sent to Event Management whenever inventory ownership is transferred from a supplier to a warehouse. For example, if you track the consignment of inventory for which the supplier maintains ownership after it is received into a warehouse, then at the point that ownership is transferred to the warehouse and is no longer the supplier’s, an event can be raised.If No, information is not sent to Event Management.

You specify the number of minutes after which, if no response has been received from Warehouse Labor Management, communication is considered to be in error and Event Management is notified.If No, information is not sent to Event Management.
If Yes, information is sent to Event Management whenever a work queue request is cancelled without being completed.If No, information is not sent to Event Management.

Warehouse Management configuration value that corresponds to the GS1 value. For example, if you are mapping dock sets, enter a dock set value as defined in WM, and then enter the corresponding GS1 dock set value in the GS1 Value field.

GS1 code value that corresponds to the Warehouse Management value. For example, if you are mapping dock sets, enter a standard GS1 dock set, and then enter the corresponding WM dock set in the WM Value field.

The cube conversion factor is used to convert a larger measurement unit (MU) for volume to a smaller MU for volume (for example, cubic feet to cubic inches). If the volume MU used by Transportation Manager is larger than the volume MU used by Warehouse Management, then enter a conversion factor. Warehouse Management converts the volume it receives from Transportation Manager by multiplying it by the cube conversion factor. For example, the factor used to convert cubic feet to cubic inches in 1728. If the volume MU is the same for both systems, enter a value of 1. See the Transportation Manager and Warehouse Management Integration Guide.

If Yes, and if Transportation Manager (TM) is integrated with Warehouse Management, then when an order line is downloaded from the host, Warehouse Management sends the order line details to Transportation Manager (such as volume and weight measurements, item family, commodity code, and a hazardous material indicator). Order line details are sent based on the scheduled job SEND-TMS-ORDER-LINE-MEASURES; jobs are maintained in the Console, under Jobs.When the scheduled job runs, the system sends the details for all of the order lines on the order to TM through an integrator transaction (ORDER_UPDATE_TO_CANONICAL). TM uses the details to estimate and plan loads more accurately before sending load plan information back to Warehouse Management. On the Outbound page, you can filter order lines to view only those for which details have not yet been sent to Transportation Manager (Pending to TM field).Note: If updates are made to an order line prior to the job running, then the updated information is sent to TM. If updates to an order line are downloaded after the order line details have been sent to TM, the updated order line details are not sent unless another new order line is downloaded, and the details are sent again.If No, then order line details are not sent to Transportation Manager.
If Enabled, Warehouse Labor Management functionality is available for use in Warehouse Management.If Disabled, then Warehouse Labor Management functionality it is not available for use.

Service URL of the Warehouse Labor Management instance with which you want to integrate Warehouse Management. Only required if Warehouse Labor Management is installed in a separate instance from Warehouse Management.

If Yes, then when a user logs out of Warehouse Management, a message is displayed asking if it is the end of the day. The application uses this message to determine whether to send a transaction to Warehouse Labor Management when the user logs out.If you choose to have the message displayed, then you can also select whether an IEND or ISTOP transaction is sent when the user answers Yes to the message.If No, no message is displayed.

Type of transaction that is sent when the user answers Yes to the end of day message. The end of day message is a notice that is displayed when the user logs out of Warehouse Management; the message typically asks the user if it is the end of their work day. If the user answers No to the end of day message, no transaction is sent is when user logs out.• IEND: Transaction that indicates the end of the user's activities in Warehouse Management, and allows the ISTOP (end of the day) transaction to be sent by another system when the user punches out. • ISTOP: Transaction that indicates the end of the user's work day.

field: Send Labor Data for Unmeasured Users
description: If Yes, labor data is sent to Warehouse Labor Management for users that are configured as Unmeasured. An unmeasured user is typically a user for whom labor tracking is not required, such as a seasonal or temporary employee, or a new employee during a probationary period.If No, labor data is not sent for users configured as Unmeasured.
If Yes, locations are built jointly between Warehouse Labor Management and Warehouse Management.If No, locations are not built jointly between the applications.

If Yes, you want Warehouse Labor Management to provide goal time estimates for picks, pick work assignments, putaway, and replenishments. Set Labor Goal Time to Yes to enable Warehouse Labor Management to calculate the goal time estimates for picks, pick work assignments, putaway, and replenishments. Goal time estimates are calculated by creating Future Assignments in Warehouse Labor Management.Goal time calculations should be considered estimates because they can change based on multiple factors, such as skipped picks, use of different travel sequences, and transition move travel time. The following goal time calculation exceptions exist:• The goal time calculation does not factor in transition moves because those moves can only be calculated when the actual work happens. That time is reflected in Actual Assignments. • While goal times can be calculated for both directed and undirected work, they cannot be calculated for putaway work that is performed immediately. A putaway work task must exist in the work queue in order for Warehouse Management to send the assignment details, such as the destination location, to Warehouse Labor Management for goal time calculation.• Goal time calculation is not available when a user picks more than one work reference without depositing the previous pick. In this case, the Summary screen displays Goal Time as "N/A".• The goal time estimated for a threshold pick is less than the actual goal time because the location to which excess inventory is deposited is unknown until it occurs. • Goal time cannot be calculated for a manual replenishment. • Goal times are not available when the warehouse transfer is in progress.If No, goal time estimates are not displayed.

Defines the number of days in advance of the arrival of an inbound shipment when labor planning for the inbound shipment should be performed.For example, you can set the value for Receive Pre Plan Days to 2. Then, if the expected date of an inbound shipment is January 12, WLM initiates planning for the inbound shipment on January 10. If the value for Receive Pre Plan Days is less than 0, planning will be disabled regardless of the expected date of an inbound shipment.
If Yes, WLM provides pick goal time estimates for order lines.If No, pick goal times for order lines are not displayed.

If Yes, Warehouse Management will defer sending pick information to Warehouse Labor Management by using a background process. If you choose to defer the information, you must also configure a background process to send the deferred information to Warehouse Labor Management.If No, Warehouse Management will send pick information to Warehouse Labor Management immediately during the pick release process. If you choose to send the information immediately, the pick release process in Warehouse Management could slow down significantly.

field: Limit Locations For Movement Cost Calculation
description: If Yes, then the number of locations that are sent by Warehouse Management (WM) to Warehouse Labor Management (WLM) for cost movement calculations is limited to the value you define in the Maximum Locations For Movement Cost Calculation field. Movement cost calculation is used to determine the best location to deposit a piece of inventory when WM attempts to allocate a location during a system-directed inventory move. During this calculation, WLM considers the device and equipment of the operator as well as the travel distances between the source location and eligible destination locations sent by WM.IMPORTANT: Limiting the number of locations considered for movement cost calculation can reduce processing time when WM and WLM are installed in separate instances, especially if the WLM instance is on a remote server. However, this setting has no effect on system performance when WM and WLM are installed in the same instance.If you do not limit the number of locations or you set the limit too high, the processing time for movement cost calculation will increase. A lower limit will decrease the processing time, however, only the limited number of locations will have an actual calculated movement cost. For example, if a large facility with thousands of locations does not set a limit, then each time the system attempts to find a deposit location for inventory, WM sends every eligible deposit location (for the operation) to WLM for movement cost calculation. Alternatively, if limiting is enabled and the Maximum Locations For Movement Cost Calculation field value is 100, then WM sends only the first 100 locations for movement calculations to determine the best location; the first 100 locations are selected using the configured location sorting settings for the current operations, such as putaway. Set this field to Yes and define a limit to avoid a significant decrease in system performance during system-directed inventory movements.If No, then the number of locations that WM sends to WLM for movement cost calculation is unlimited.

field: Maximum Locations For Movement Cost Calculation
description: Maximum number of locations that Warehouse Management (WM) sends to Warehouse Labor Management (WLM) for movement cost calculation. Movement cost calculation is used to determine the best location to deposit a piece of inventory when WM attempts to allocate a location during a system-directed inventory move. During this calculation, WLM considers the device and equipment of the operator as well as the travel distances between the source location and eligible destination locations sent by WM.IMPORTANT: Limiting the number of locations considered for movement cost calculation can reduce processing time when WM and WLM are installed in separate instances, especially if the WLM instance is on a remote server. However, this setting has no effect on system performance when WM and WLM are installed in the same instance.If you do not limit the number of locations or you set the limit too high, the processing time for movement cost calculation will increase. A lower limit will decrease the processing time, however, only the limited number of locations will have an actual calculated movement cost. For example, if a large facility with thousands of locations does not set a limit, then each time the system attempts to find a deposit location for inventory, WM sends every eligible deposit location (for the operation) to WLM for movement cost calculation. Alternatively, if the limit is set at 100, then WM sends only the first 100 locations for movement cost calculation to determine the best location; the first 100 locations are selected using the configured location sorting settings for the current operations, such as putaway. You use this limit to avoid a significant decrease in system performance during system-directed inventory movements.

If Yes, you want to use the labor planning feature for work orders. Enabling the labor planning feature for work orders means that Warehouse Management will send work order information when a work order is automatically generated from a host transaction download or from a bill of material (BOM) with the Auto-generate Work Order check box selected, or when the goal time for a work order is manually requested. Warehouse Labor Management uses the work order information to create planning assignments and estimated goal times for the associated work orders.If No, labor planning processing is disabled.

If Yes, Warehouse Management will defer sending work order information to Warehouse Labor Management when a work order is automatically generated from a host transaction download or from a bill of material with the Auto-generate Work Order check box selected, or when the goal time for a work order is manually requested. Instead, it will be sent later by a background process. If you choose to defer the information, you must also configure a background process to send the deferred information to Warehouse Labor Management.If No, Warehouse Management will send work order information to Warehouse Labor Management immediately (when a work order is automatically generated from a host transaction download or from a bill of material with the Auto-generate Work Order check box selected, or when the goal time for a work order is manually requested). If you choose to send the information immediately, the work order process in Warehouse Management could slow down significantly.

field: Release Appointment Picks By Labor Estimate
description: If Yes, picks are released in advance of an appointment date and time so that all of the inventory can be picked and loaded in time for the shipping transport equipment to meet its scheduled dispatch time. Labor planning must also be enabled.If No, the pick release by labor estimate process is disabled.

Additional amount of time to add to the total time in which to release picks to allow for additional time for activities such as processing paperwork or preparing the inventory for shipment. The additional amount of time can either be a percent or number of minutes. See the Buffer Time Calculate By field.

Option indicating how the number in the Buffer Time field is to be used in calculating additional time.• Percent: Calculate the additional time as a percentage of the Warehouse Labor Management goal time and add the result. For example, if the Buffer Time is 10, the Buffer Time Calculated By is Percent and the Warehouse Labor Management goal time is 600, then the total time frame is 660 seconds [600 + (10% x 600)].• Minutes: Add the additional time as straight minutes to the Warehouse Labor Management goal time. For example, if the Buffer Time is 10, the Buffer Time Calculated By is Minutes and the Warehouse Labor Management goal time is 600, then the total time frame is 1200 seconds [600 + (10 minutes x 60 seconds/minute)].
Date and time to use as the deadline for loading the transport equipment. If this field is left blank, then the application defaults to Start Date.

Additional amount of time to add to the total time in which to release picks. This is to allow for additional time for activities such as processing paperwork or preparing the inventory for shipment. For example, if the Buffer Time is 10, the Buffer Time Calculated By is Minutes and the Warehouse Labor Management goal time is 600, then the total time frame is 1200 seconds [600 + (10 minutes x 60 seconds/minute)].
